data.title: Plastic bag bans and fees reduce harmful bag litter on shorelines
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料袋禁令及其环境影响，特别是对海滩和海洋污染的影响

不同观点：
• **Hedora**：认为加州的塑料袋禁令虽然减少了塑料袋的数量，但导致了更重的“可重复使用”塑料袋的广泛使用。这些袋子含更多塑料，需要更长时间降解，实际上增加了塑料污染。他主张应针对没有塑料替代品的产品进行禁令，而非目前的最有效使用塑料的产品。

• **Ofalkaed**：住在海滩附近，认为塑料袋从未是主要问题。真正的问题是人们随意丢弃垃圾，尤其是在禁令后不再用塑料袋装垃圾，导致垃圾遍地。特别是尿布被随意丢弃，成为更严重的问题。

• **Thinkingemote**：指出大多数海滩上的塑料来自海洋，主要源于航运、渔业和工业，而非海滩游客。认为需要全面看待海洋污染问题。

• **Mykowebhn**：对公众对塑料废物问题的关注度低感到失望，指出视频游戏销售等话题更受关注。认为需要激发公众参与环保的意愿。

• **B0a04gl**：批评仅通过数量而非重量来衡量塑料污染的政策是表面功夫，指出如果新塑料袋更厚，则污染问题并未解决。

• **Drakonka**：个人经验表明，当塑料袋收费后，改用布袋是立即的解决方案，偶尔使用纸袋。

• **Cubefox**：指出大多数海洋塑料来自特定国家，其他国家贡献较少，认为这是执法问题而非不可解决的。

• **Culebron21**：质疑塑料瓶和吸管的污染问题，指出这些也可能在污染中占重要位置。

• **Unlimit**：支持全面禁止塑料袋。

• **Yboris**：指出渔网是海洋塑料的主要来源，呼吁减少鱼类消费以帮助解决此问题。

• **Keybored**：认为塑料袋垃圾数量下降是因为消费者在结账时有选择，但许多产品包装中的塑料难以避免，应集中解决消费者选择相关的塑料污染。

• **Userbinator**：担心全面禁止有害物品会走向威权主义，质疑当前路径。

• **Jekwoooooe**：认为用棉布或聚酯袋替代塑料袋对环境整体更不利，批评这是“左倾”情感逻辑，而非实际改善。

补充讨论：
- **政策效果争议**：Hedora与Ofalkaed对禁令效果有争议，前者关注塑料总量增加，后者关注实际垃圾处理问题。
- **污染源的多样性**：Thinkingemote和Cubefox强调海洋污染的多样性和复杂性，指出不仅仅是塑料袋问题。
- **替代品的环境影响**：Jekwoooooe和Drakonka讨论了替代品的环境成本和实用性。
- **公众参与和意识**：Mykowebhn强调了提高公众环保意识的重要性。

争议焦点：塑料袋禁令是否有效减少了整体塑料污染，以及替代品的环境和实际使用效果。

data.title: Life as Slime
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了生命起源的早期猜想以及现代科学对生命独特性和稀有性的认识。19世纪，德国医生Ferdinand von Ritgen认为最早的人类胚胎像真菌一样从泥土中自发生长，这种想法在当时具有一定合理性。然而，随着达尔文进化论的提出和科学进步，这类猜想被逐渐取代。尽管如此，一些著名科学家如史蒂芬·霍金仍将人类描述为“化学污垢”。现代科学努力在实验室中创造人工生命，并搜索外星生命，但迄今未成功，显示生命可能极为罕见。因此，将生命视为“仅仅是泥浆中的真菌”这一观点需要重新审视，因为生命或许是宇宙中独特而珍贵的现象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“生命是星球上的黏液”这一说法的不同理解和讨论，涉及生命在宇宙中的意义、生命的复杂性与稀有性，以及该比喻是否恰当。

不同观点：
• necovek认为，霍金的说法强调的是生命相对于宇宙的渺小，而不是生命本身的美丽或复杂性。他认为即使生命的复杂性令人惊叹，但与宇宙的广阔相比仍然微不足道。此外，人类可能永远无法体验宇宙中其他可能存在的奇妙现象。

Prominent scientists continue to claim life is “just” slime on a spinning rock. However, in an age when the rarity and fragility of life are increasingly evident, it’s time to retire the metaphor.

This article concludes Issue 06. Watch our Behind-the-Scenes interview with the author
on YouTube
.
By
Thomas Moynihan
In 1832, Ferdinand von Ritgen, a German physician,
puzzled over
how the first generation of humans birthed themselves. He
pictured their
embryos sprouting spontaneously “without procreating parents preceding them,” like fungal growths emerging from the ground.
By Ritgen’s day, it was understood that life on Earth had predated humanity’s debut for eons and that living creatures had increased in complexity across that duration — but it wasn’t understood how novel forms appeared. A twenty-two-year-old Charles Darwin had boarded
the HMS Beagle
only a year before, his theory of evolution as yet unconceived. Given available knowledge, Ritgen’s conjecture made sense.
A seasoned obstetrician, Ritgen knew firsthand the intricacies and difficulties of childbirth. As there would have been neither mothers nor uteruses to incubate these first fetuses, he reasoned that nature must have provided substitutes. He imagined seedpods sprouting around the fetuses, cupping them like protective wombs. Ritgen claimed these would have resembled the fleshy blossoms of
Rafflesia arnoldii
, better known as the “stinking corpse lily” because of how it emulates the smell of corporeal decay to attract pollinators.
A detailed illustration of a Rafflesia flower by the Scottish botanist, Robert Brown, who introduced the genus to the scientific world in 1820. Credit: Biodiversity Heritage Library.
Ritgen
pictured
the “first child awakening in the calyx” of this “gigantic flower,” swimming in the amniotic bliss of its “milky sap.” These “leathery” chalices,
he remarked
, would have germinated in “
Uferschlamm
,” the riverside mud. He pointed to countless other organisms that seemed to emerge, without prior parents, from slime: mites, algae, jellyfish, lice, and even intestinal worms. At the time, the idea of gestation without prior procreation had
not yet been
satisfactorily disproven.
Of course, some weren’t impressed. Theologians decried that by implying we weren’t descended from Adam, Ritgen
demoted us
to “fungus-people” with a pedigree that was but a nativity of slime. They
deemed his idea
yet another noxious fruit of scientific “nihilism,” budding alongside all the other godless theories shooting up “like disgusting mushrooms in the pathologically productive soil of our time.”
Ignoring Ritgen’s excusable ignorance of the Darwinian steps that separated slime from simian, his basic sentiment lives on today. Even the eminent Stephen Hawking, appearing on a 1995
BBC documentary
about cosmology, voiced
the motif
before the credits rolled: “The human race is just a chemical scum on a moderate-sized planet, orbiting around a very average star in the outer suburb of one among a hundred billion galaxies.” Hawking delivered this assertion with the vestige of a grin.
For many centuries, misanthropes and humanists alike have indulged in similar comparisons. But this argument has metamorphosed alongside scientific understanding. Where we used to think life was overabundant, we now recognize that it may be staggeringly rare.
Biotechnologists know this firsthand. Several decades of effort to create “artificial life” in the laboratory have produced
biochemical machines
and
self-sustained protein production systems
but, as yet, no organisms capable of cell division or robust metabolism. Astronomers, similarly, have scoured outer space for signs of life
since 1960
, and still haven’t found convincing evidence of biology beyond Earth’s atmosphere — though
the search continues
.
So, is it right to say biology is “
just
” a planetary fungal infection? The answer, as it turns out, depends on whether the “just” disparages something lowly or underscores something breathtakingly unique.

Life’s Effortless Origins
Our understanding of life’s cosmic place and prevalence has evolved since Ritgen’s time. As his conjecture reveals, the defining boundary between organic and inorganic was once quite blurry. Visions of animals naturally springing from wet mud go back to the pre-Stoic philosopher Anaximander, but Ritgen had been more immediately preceded by Lorenz Oken, another German naturalist who argued all life comes from “
Urschleim,
” the primordial slime.
An 1870 illustration by Ernst Haeckel of the primordial ocean slime, or “Urschleim,” from which he believed all life emerged. Credit: Biodiversity Her

data.title: Scaling our observability platform by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
data.author: valyala
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者的内部观测平台如何从19 PiB增长到超过100 PB，处理近500万亿行数据，并成功应对了20倍事件量增长，同时CPU使用率减少到原来的10%以下。尽管OpenTelemetry（OTel）在初期有效，但随着数据规模和复杂性的增加，OTel成为瓶颈。为此，作者开发了自定义管道（SysEx），以更好地满足高性能需求，并引入了基于ClickHouse的HyperDX，提供更高效的观测体验。最终，作者转向ClickStack，这是一个围绕ClickHouse构建的端到端观测堆栈，旨在提升数据探索和根因分析的效率。文章总结了在大规模数据场景下，OTel的局限性和自定义解决方案的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日志记录和数据存储的有效性、工具选择及其实现的优缺点

不同观点：
• **日志数据量与存储效率的争议**：[b0a04gl] 认为存储 100PB 的日志数据只是表明尚未明确哪些数据值得记录，建议通过自动化修剪未被查询或未触发警报的日志来减少存储浪费。而 [henning] 指出记录所有事件会大大增加存储成本，但这一成本常常被忽略。

• **工具的适用性**：[jurgenkesker] 认为该讨论主要与 ClickHouse 日志收集相关，对其他日志不具实际意义，尽管个人喜欢 ClickHouse。而 [iw7tdb2kqo9] 则质疑在 ClickHouse 规模下是否可以有效查询日志数据，并比较了 ClickHouse 与 ElasticSearch 及 JSON 文件存储的区别。

• **日志系统在服务故障时的表现**：[mrbluecoat] 强调 OpenTelemetry 在服务失败状态下仍能捕获日志，而 SysEx 无法在服务不可用时收集数据，这对于事故分析至关重要。[Thaxll] 进一步指出，如果服务宕机时无法获取日志，整个解决方案就无意义。

• **数据存储与生态系统的标准化问题**：[revskill] 认为当前行业标准多为半成品或仍在发展中，导致生态系统分割，且制定标准的过程多为试错法，不够严谨。[atemerev] 则通过对比 ClickHouse 和 Postgres，表达了对数据处理效率的惊讶。

• **环保与数据浪费的关注**：[ofrzeta] 认为大量生成和存储数据是浪费资源，建议减少数据创建量，暗示当前做法存在环境和资源利用上的问题。

• **技术实现细节**：[the_real_cher] 对 ClickHouse 和 Dynamo 使用的技术（如大型哈希表）表示好奇。[tjungblut] 简要总结了技术改进，如零拷贝处理原始字节以替代 JSON 序列化与反序列化。

补充讨论：
• **日志保留时间与数据聚合问题**：[the_arun] 提到日志保留时间的重要性，并质疑在长时间后是否仍需保留原始数据，还是仅保留汇总数据即可。

• **对 observability maximalism 的批评**：[jappgar] 认为过度追求可观察性是一种浪费资源的“崇拜”行为，暗示其成本效益不高。

Scaling our Observability platform beyond 100 Petabytes by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
Rory Crispin
Jun 19, 2025
-
32
minutes read
TLDR
#
Observability at scale:
Our internal system grew from 19 PiB to 100 PB of uncompressed logs and from ~40 trillion to 500 trillion rows.
Efficiency breakthrough:
We absorbed a 20× surge in event volume using under 10% of the CPU previously needed.
OTel pitfalls:
The required parsing and marshalling of events in OpenTelemetry proved a bottleneck and didn’t scale - our custom pipeline addressed this.
Introducing HyperDX:
ClickHouse-native observability UI for seamless exploration, correlation, and root-cause analysis with Lucene-like syntax.
Introduction
#
About a year ago, we
shared the story of LogHouse
- our internal logging platform built to monitor ClickHouse Cloud. At the time, it managed what felt like a massive 19 PiB of data. More than just solving our observability challenges, LogHouse also saved us millions by replacing an increasingly unsustainable Datadog bill. The response to that post was overwhelming. It was clear our experience resonated with others facing similar struggles with traditional observability vendors and underscored just how critical effective data management is at scale.
A year later, LogHouse has grown beyond anything we anticipated and is now storing over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data across nearly 500 trillion rows. That kind of scale forced a series of architectural changes, new tools, and hard-earned lessons that we felt were worth sharing - not least that OpenTelemetry (OTel) isn’t always the panacea of Observability (though we still love it), and that sometimes custom pipelines are essential.
In our case, this shift enabled us to handle a 20x increase in event volume using less than 10% of the CPU for our most critical data source - a transformation with massive implications for cost and efficiency.
Other parts of our stack have also changed, not least due to the
ClickHouse acquisition of HyperDX
. Not only did this give us a first-party ClickHouse-native UI, but it also led to the
creation of ClickStack
- an opinionated, end-to-end observability stack built around ClickHouse. With HyperDX, we’ve started transitioning away from our Grafana-based custom UI, moving toward a more integrated experience for exploration, correlation, and root cause analysis.
As more teams adopt ClickHouse for observability and realize just how much they can store and query affordably, we hope these insights prove as useful as our first post. If you’re curious about this journey, when and where OTel is appropriate, and how we scaled a log pipeline to 100PB…read on.
Get started today
Interested in seeing how ClickHouse works on your data? Get started with ClickHouse Cloud in minutes and receive $300 in free credits.
Sign up
Beyond general purpose: evolving observability at scale
#
Over the past year, our approach to observability has undergone a significant transformation. We've continued to leverage OpenTelemetry to gather general-purpose logs, but as our systems have scaled, we began to reach its limits. While OTel remains a valuable part of our toolkit, it couldn't fully deliver the performance and precision we needed for our most demanding workloads. This prompted us to develop purpose-built tools tailored to our critical systems and rethink where generic solutions truly fit. Along the way, we've broadened the range of data we collect and revamped how we present insights to engineers.
A new frontier of scale
#
When we last wrote about LogHouse, we were proud to handle 19 PiB of uncompressed data across 37 trillion rows. Today, those numbers feel like a distant memory. LogHouse now stores over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data, representing nearly 500 trillion rows.
Here's a quick look at the breakdown:
System
Uncompressed Size
Stored rows
SysEx

OTel

16.7 Trillion
These numbers also tell a story. In our original post, 100% of our telemetry flowed through OpenTelemetry, with every log line collected via the same general-purpose pipeline. But as the scale and complexity of our data grew, so did the need for specialization.
While our total volume has grown more than 5x, the breakdown reveals a deliberate shift in strategy: today, the vast majority of our data comes from “SysEx”, a new purpose-built exporter we developed to handle high-throughput, high-fidelity system logs from ClickHouse itself. This shift marks a turning point in how we think about observability pipelines - and brings us to our first key topic.
We hope the following helps comprehend the scale at which LogHouse operates.
OpenTelemetry's efficiency challenges at extreme scale
#
Initially, we used OpenTelemetry (OTel) for all log collection. It was a great starting point and an established industry standard which allowed us to quickly establish a baseline where every pod in our Kubernetes environment shipped logs to ClickHouse.

data.title: Delta Chat is a decentralized and secure messenger app
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Delta Chat是一款去中心化且安全的即时通讯应用，支持多账户和多设备，用户可选择使用安全快速的聊天邮件服务器或传统电子邮件服务器。它提供互动式网页应用，适用于游戏和协作，并经过审核的端到端加密，防止网络和服务器攻击。该软件是自由开源软件（FOSS），基于互联网标准构建，避免了xkcd927问题。支持移动和桌面设备，提供多语言版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Delta Chat及其相关技术的优缺点，包括去中心化聊天工具的安全性、隐私性、可迁移性及其实现技术。

不同观点：
• **ZoomZoomZoom**：认为Delta Chat等去中心化工具虽然利用了现有基础设施，但依赖特定服务器，存在用户被切断服务器后难以迁移的问题。建议使用密钥对作为用户标识，以实现无缝的服务器切换，避免因国家审查导致账号失效。

• **heavyset_go**：指出Delta Chat基于IMAP和SMTP协议，虽然能保证消息内容的安全，但在隐私和匿名性方面表现不足。邮件系统本身并非为隐私设计，因此Delta Chat不适合用于身份和社交图谱的隐藏。

• **maqp**：强调Delta Chat缺乏完美前向安全性（PFS），如果私钥泄露，历史消息可能被解密。相比之下，Signal协议更为安全，因此不建议使用安全性较差的应用。

• **sixtiethutopia**：提到Delta Chat使用PGP加密，但不支持前向安全性，并且在收到未加密消息时会自动切换到未加密通信。还担心可能会受到降级攻击，即 adversaries 通过伪造发送地址使通信降级为未加密。

• **shark_laser**：推荐使用0xchat，它基于Nostr协议，支持私钥登录、加密聊天和闪电支付，具备去中心化和跨平台特性。

• **raybb**：关注用户在迁移到不同服务器时，是否能保持原有聊天记录，指出这是类似WhatsApp的痛点。

• **blancotech**：开玩笑地将Delta Chat与Delta航空公司混淆，表现出对其他类型聊天系统的兴趣。

data.title: Cosmoe: BeOS Class Library on Top of Wayland
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: Cosmoe 是一款新的 C++ UI 库，旨在为 Wayland 创建易于开发且资源消耗低的图形应用程序。它将 BeOS 类库的优势带入现代内核和显示引擎，具有易用、多线程和高性能的特点。目前，Cosmoe 仍处于开发阶段，作为源代码技术预览提供，用户需要从 GitLab 下载并编译代码。未来的改进重点包括稳定性和兼容性，目标是实现完整的 BeOS API 支持。Cosmoe 基于 MIT 许可证发布，是 Haiku 操作系统的一个分支，而当前版本与之前的 "Cosmoe Classic" 不同，后者是 Haiku 到 Linux 内核的完整移植。开发者正专注于共享库版本的开发，以实现最大的实用价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BeOS/Haiku操作系统的设计及其现代应用

不同观点：
• **对BeOS/Haiku设计的高度赞赏**：
   - leonheld认为BeOS/Haiku代表了计算机设计的巅峰，对其美学表示赞赏。
   - pjerem和imchillyb表达了对BeOS设计理念的喜爱，尤其是其技术预览和用户友好性。

• **对文件系统和扩展属性的技术讨论**：
   - sockboy和em-bee讨论了通过模拟文件系统的扩展属性来进行轻量级操作系统定制的方法，并探讨了是否需要完整移植文件系统驱动以实现BeOS的文件系统特性。
   - em-bee特别关注BeOS风格的窗口管理器和数据库式文件系统，并对命令行工具的可用性感兴趣。

• **对BeOS API的实现和历史回顾**：
   - dkh提到BeOS API的实现可能是对抗Wayland反对者的“杀手级应用”。
   - jbverschoor分享了早期在win32 API上实现BeOS API的经历，希望借此推动BeOS的普及。

• **对Haiku项目进展的评价**：
   - tialaramex调侃Haiku项目的缓慢进展，指出其历经四分之一个世纪仍未接近发布正式版本。

• **对实际应用和开发者支持的关注**：
   - jchw对BeOS API的UI设计表示赞赏，但担心缺乏基本的无障碍支持，认为这是一个严重问题。
   - imchillyb提到BeOS和其他类似项目（如Microsoft phones、Pebble watch）缺乏开发者支持的问题，强调需要有意义的参与而不仅仅是短暂的惊艳。

• **对现有UI库的比较**：
   - kosolam质疑该库的实际好处，指出已有众多UI库（如gtk、qt、fltk、wx等），并询问其独特之处。

补充讨论：
• **BeOS的历史和影响**：
   - danans提到BeOS被Palm收购，并进一步发展为WebOS，最后被LG收购，询问BeOS特性是否影响当前的LG电视。

• **其他简短评论**：
   - Apocryphon认为这是比Liquid Glass更令人兴奋的UI新闻。
   - mouse_简单表达了对该项目的喜爱。

争议焦点：
• **Haiku项目进展缓慢**：部分评论对Haiku项目历经多年仍未有实质性进展表示调侃和批评。
• **开发者支持和实际应用**：对BeOS及类似项目缺乏开发者支持和有意义应用的担忧。

总结：讨论围绕BeOS/Haiku的设计美学、技术实现、历史演变及其现代应用展开，涉及文件系统、API实现、项目进展和实际应用等多方面问题。

Frequently Asked Questions
How can I try out Cosmoe?
Cosmoe is still a work in progress, and exists as a source-only technology preview for now.  To run it, clone or download the
Cosmoe source code repo from Gitlab
and compile the code on your Linux distribution of choice.  There are several sample applications included which demonstrate what it is capable of.
What are the plans for Cosmoe going forward?
Cosmoe needs 2 main improvements to be a reliable, full-featured UI library:
Stability
While I've made incredible strides with getting the BeOS class libraries to talk to Wayland, much work still remains to weed out crashes and incorrect behavior.  Wayland is powerful, but not friendly.
Compatibility
Cosmoe implements about 95% of the BeOS API currently.  Notable feature that are not yet implemented include "offscreen" BBitmaps for accelerated drawing, and BFilePanel which implements Open and Save dialog boxes.  Some file-related classes like BVolume are only partially implemented.  Also, for security reasons, Wayland forbids certain Window-related actions such as window positioning and centering, so that functionality can never exist.
For more details on this items and other in-progress aspects of Cosmoe, please see the
TODO file in the Cosmoe repo
.
What license does Cosmoe use?
Cosmoe is distributed under the MIT license.
What source code comprises Cosmoe?  Where did it come from, and what inspired it?
Cosmoe is a fork of the Haiku operating system, which itself is an open-source re-implementation of BeOS.  The current iteration of Cosmoe is implemented as a UI library, but
the previous iteration (now known as "Cosmoe Classic")
was a full port of Haiku to the Linux kernel.
How is the current iteration of Cosmoe different from Cosmoe Classic?
The
current iteration of Cosmoe
is a shared library which implements the BeOS class library on top of Wayland.  There are no supporting programs, e.g. app_server or registrar, needed to use it.  All the necessary functionality is rolled into the library.  Apps linked with the library run natively on Linux via Wayland.
The
previous iteration of Cosmoe (now known as "Cosmoe Classic")
is a full port of the Haiku OS to the Linux kernel.  It runs inside an SDL window on Linux.  It would be possible to develop graphics drivers to allow it to run as its own standalone Linux-based OS, but those have not been developed.
Moving forward, my focus is on the shared library version since I believe it has the most practical benefit.

不同观点：
• [ajb] 认为原帖缺乏细节，并提供了法语文章链接以及国际输血协会（ISBT）的相关页面链接，指出ISBT已将新血液类型添加到他们的列表中，尽管页面显示仍为47种，但数据表中已更新。
• [kimos] 表示对血液类型数量的理解一直停留在约8种，发现有48种非常令人震惊。
• [kalium-xyz] 认为血液类型问题在大多数情况下不重要，但在某些情况下却至关重要。
• [tetris11] 对新血液类型被命名为PIGZ表示好奇。
• [escapecharacter] 调侃说，动漫粉丝维基可能会因此疯狂更新。

补充讨论：
• [thaumasiotes] 对新血液类型发现如何帮助解释某些病理现象表示疑问，特别是当三个兄弟姐妹因罕见血液类型而出现风湿病症状时，文章未详细说明他们是否定期接受输血。

data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 文章报道了詹姆斯·库克船长的船只**奋进号**（HMS Endeavour）的残骸在美国罗德岛新港港湾被发现。这艘船在1768至1771年间成为首艘抵达澳大利亚东部的欧洲船只，后在美国独立战争期间更名为“桑德wich勋爵”号并沉没。经过25年的考古研究，澳大利亚国立海事博物馆确认了残骸的身份，尽管此前有合作伙伴对初步报告提出质疑。沉船中的文物稀少，但所有发现均与18世纪相符。该船在战争中被用作运输和监狱船，并与其他12艘船一同被故意凿沉以阻挡港口。

From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
Your support makes all the difference.
Read more
The remains of captain
Cook
’s ship,
HMS Endeavour
,
has been located
off the US coast after sinking 250 years ago.
Between 1768 and 1771, the ship became the first European
vessel
to reach eastern Australia. It was then sold and renamed the Lord
Sandwich
before sinking off the US coast
during the American War of Independence in 1778.
For
centuries the ship was lost
, but now the wreck has been found in Newport Harbour,
Rhode Island
.
The finding was announced in a
new report
by the Australian National Maritime Museum (ANMM) and experts have identified the wreck as RI 2394.
Daryl Karp, Museum director explained the findings in the report are the result of 25 years of archaeological research and underwater investigations.
open image in gallery
Edward Fage, [Newport and its environs, ca. 1778], William L. Clements Library, University of Michigan, 8380. Note ‘Sunken Ships’ indicated due west of North Battery (circled)
(
Australian National Maritime Museum
)
The shipwreck was compared to historic plans for Cook’s ship revealing measurements aligned with those taken of a 1768 survey.
Kieran Hosty, ANMM archaeologist, who co-wrote the report, said: “The timbers are British timbers. The size of all the timber scantlings are almost identical to
Endeavour
, and I’m talking within millimetres - not inches, but millimetres.
“The stem scarf is identical, absolutely identical. This stem scarf is also a very unique feature - we’ve gone through a whole bunch of 18th-century ship’s plans, and we can’t find anything else like it.”
The ship was used for British troop transport and a prison ship in the American War of Independence. In this time, it was renamed Lord Sandwich.
When American and French besieged Newport Harbour the ship was one of 13 vessels deliberately sunk to act as a submerged blockage. It was never salvaged and remained sank.
open image in gallery
Mosaic showing frame and scuttling hole beneath letter board, north is at bottom of image (John D. Broadwater)
(
Australian National Maritime Museum
)
Archaeologist James Hunter, co-author of the report, explained that it was unlikely they would find artefacts that would provide an immediate identification. Anything that was of value would have been taken out of the ship before it sank.
However, everything experts have found so far is indicative of the 18th century.
The finding comes after a preliminary report in 2022, identified the same wreck as the
HMS Endeavour
. But it was met with criticism by the museum’s research partners, the Rhode Island Marine Archaeology Project (RIMAP) who said the finding was “premature” and a “breach of contract”, claiming that it was the lead organisation for the study, The Telegraph reported.
In a statement, ANMM said it was not ruling out other candidate shipwreck sites.

data.title: On memes, mimetic desire, and why it's always that deep
data.author: lawrenceyan
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文化现象的批判性分析与个人享受之间的关系，以及个体在社会结构中的行为模式。

不同观点：
• [rixed] 认为人们缺乏通过集体行动解决结构性问题的工具，因此往往通过个人道德视角解读这些问题。他还提出，人们通过情感捷径（如符号和道德）相互影响，而不是通过知识。
   
• [Apreche] 认为人们无法质疑自己为何享受某些事物，并将批判性思考与道德谴责混为一谈。他强调自己会严格区分道德判断与质量判断，并认为大多数人无法回答“为什么喜欢某物”的问题。

• [NoboruWataya] 指出对流行文化的深度分析可能有趣且有益，但过度消费这些内容会让人疲惫。他认为，许多流行事物受欢迎正是因为不需要过多思考，过度分析可能削弱享受。他主张人们应根据需要选择是否接触这些分析内容。

• [57473m3n7Fur7h3] 提到在移动端阅读时，由于排版问题，误将号召性内容当作引用，造成困惑。

• [shayway] 享受批判性分析，但认为有些人将这种分析视为道德要求是不合理的。他主张分析的动机应是乐趣，而非道德优越感，并强调好奇心应自然产生，而非被强加。

• [strken] 认为“让人们享受事物”的观点常被用作无法准确反驳时的托辞。他批评对资本主义的无差别批判，指出这种批判的泛滥使其失去说服力。

• [blamestross] 认为 meme 是压缩的沟通形式，通过文化和情境解压缩，让人感到温暖和能动性。

• [mensetmanusman] 提出个体主义的衰落是由于人口结构变化，认为这种心态不会延续到2070年以后。

• [g-r-a-y-d] 简单表达了对火车的喜爱，未参与主要讨论。

补充讨论：
• 引用了 René Girard 的复杂哲学观点，探讨模仿欲望、个体性与冲突的关系，进一步丰富了对文化和个体行为的理解。

争议焦点：
• 是否应通过批判性分析质疑文化现象，还是允许人们不加思考地享受事物。
• 批判性分析是否应被视为一种道德要求，或者仅仅是一种个人选择和乐趣。
• 对资本主义的无差别批判是否有效，以及这种批判是否削弱了分析的说服力。

data.title: Using Microsoft's New CLI Text Editor on Ubuntu
data.author: jandeboevrie
data.article_summary: Microsoft发布了开源命令行文本编辑器**Edit**，是旧版MS-DOS Editor的现代化重制版，使用Rust编写，旨在提供类似VS Code的界面和输入控制。Edit主要面向Windows用户，因为Windows缺乏内置的CLI文本编辑器，但它也可以在Linux和macOS上运行。Edit功能简洁，主打速度和简易性，支持查找替换、字词换行、多文件编辑等基本功能，但没有语法高亮或配色方案。它采用无模式设计，支持鼠标和键盘操作，易于上手。目前，Edit没有官方的Linux安装程序，但可通过GitHub或Snap安装。未来计划加入更多功能，但核心仍是轻量级文本编辑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Edit文本编辑器在不同操作系统上的使用、技术实现、历史背景及相关工具的讨论

不同观点：
• simonw：分享了如何通过Docker在macOS上运行Edit编辑器，并提供了具体命令和参考链接，强调该方法适用于Apple silicon上的Docker用户。同时提到可以从源码编译Edit。
• felineflock：认为文章混淆了TUI和CLI的概念，指出Edit实际上是1991年MS-DOS 5中EDIT程序的重新实现，并提供了相关的历史背景，如VIM和vi编辑器的出现时间，以及其他历史上的Windows文本编辑器（如EDIT、DR-DOS EDITOR等）。
• hiAndrewQuinn：讨论了常用快捷键（如Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V）的来源和使用，认为这些快捷键应更为普及，特别是在终端中的使用。
• orsenthil：赞赏Edit的易用性和简洁性，认为Linux默认编辑器（如nano, vim, emacs）对新手不够友好，建议引入类似Edit的界面。
• seabrookmx：评价Edit功能简陋，缺乏语法高亮等功能，推荐使用micro编辑器，该编辑器支持CTRL-C/V和鼠标操作。
• czarit：对Edit项目依赖于libc而不是使用Rust社区中常用的crate（如termios）表示不解，认为这种实现方式在Rust世界中非常 unusual。
• jll29：建议将Edit别名为msedit以实现“DOS兼容性”。
• aa-jv：提到PC-Write编辑器，认为其在80年代非常强大，但如今已很少使用，建议将其移植到Linux，可能是一个有趣的项目。
• jmmv：提到自己曾写过一篇关于DOS和Windows编辑器历史的文章，正是由于微软提议重新在Windows中添加文本编辑器引发的讨论。
• posix86：希望Windows终端能够移植到Linux，特别是其对Ctrl+C功能的处理。
• k3vinw：询问Edit是否仅借用了VS Code的键盘快捷键，并希望其能支持LSP和扩展功能。
• declan_roberts：赞赏Edit的UI设计，认为其不同于vim和eMacs，并让人怀念Windows 3.0/DOS时代。
• neoden：询问截图中使用的字体。
• culebron21：提到Norton Commander及其编辑器，讨论了其继任者（如Midnight Commander和FAR Manager），并指出其使用中的一些不便之处。
• tedunangst：幽默地指出老用户对全屏终端编辑器和CLI编辑器的区分感到不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：对Edit编辑器的技术实现及其与历史编辑器的比较存在不同看法，部分用户认为Edit简化了使用体验，而另一些用户则关注其功能是否足够强大和完善。
• 历史背景：对MS-DOS时期的文本编辑器（如EDIT和PC-Write）的历史讨论，以及它们在现代操作系统中的潜在价值和移植可能性。
• 快捷键和用户界面：讨论了不同平台上快捷键的普及和一致性问题，以及Edit编辑器的UI设计对用户体验的影响。

44306892.article_content:
If you spend a lot time in a terminal on Linux you’ll have preferred command-line text editor, but Microsoft’s recently announced open-source offering, simply called
Edit
, might be worth checking out — if only so you know you’re not missing out.
Edit
is a remake/reboot of the old
MS-DOS Editor
, updated to suit current sensibilities. Built using Rust, it aims to deliver a user experience that, per its GitHub page, provides
“modern interface and input controls similar to VS Code.”
Microsoft says it made
Edit
“to provide an accessible editor that even users largely unfamiliar with terminals can easily use”
on Windows if/when needed, out-of-the-box (as recent versions of Windows do not include a CLI text editor in recent versions).
The arrival of
Edit
will mean Windows devs aren’t forced to fire up notepad.exe to make a simple shell script edit, but is there any benefit to running the app on Linux?
Note:
When I spotlight apps, tools and utilities on this blog, it’s
not
because I think you (or anyone) “MUST” use them. I simply showcase choices. Whether you choose to use them is up to you.
Why would Linux users use
Edit
?
As straightforward to use as it seems
Windows is the primary target for
Edit
since it lacks a built-in CLI text editor natively so the fact you can use
Edit
on Linux (and macOS) is more of bonus than purpose.
But if you use Linux and
VSCode
your muscle memory might like the fact
Edit
shares many of the latter’s keybindings. This could make it easier to slot in to your workflow compared to
vim
or
nano
(though I stress it’s not a replacement for either of those).
Not that only avowed VSCode fans will see the appeal.
The simplicity of the text-driven UI (TUI) makes it less complex to learn, while the speed of
Edit
, even when seeking across lines in giant 1GB+ files, is impressive — both USPs are by design.
Working with multiple files is easy enough too
Eager to avoid “how to exit vim” memes, Microsoft designed
Edit
as a modeless text editor (as opposed to a multi-mode one like Vim, where you need to learn how to activate different modes and switch between them as needed).
You can
use a mouse or a keyboard
to access menus, select lines or regions of text, position the caret, etc which makes using it feel more intuitive in use than the either/or approach of (admittedly more capable) alternatives.
Edit
offers up a modest, lightweight set of features (and an equally modest footprint: a mere 250kB out of the box, and fast file opening) including:
Find and Replace
(supports
Match Case
&
Regular Expression
)
Word wrap
on resize
(optional)
Set tab/space indentation
Set/change file encoding
Line Feed (LF) or Carriage Return + Line Feed ( CRLF)
Open multiple files
There’s pretty much all there is right now.
Edit
has no syntax highlighting, no range of colour schemes, no command prompt, and few creature comforts common in other command line text editors.
Edit
is designed to edit text, rather than handle complex task better suited to IDEs.
More features are planned, including colour schemes and a settings TUI, so the list of features will grow in time, but as Microsoft’s aim is speed and simplicity, don’t expect too many bells and whistles.
Edit
is open source so anyone can modify, contribute, package or fork it.
How to Run
Edit
on Ubuntu
Edit
is free, open source software that works on Windows, Linux and macOS (so no, you don’t need to using Windows to make use of it).
Right now there is no official “installer” for Linux, and no unofficial DEB of PPA, though
there is a snap
. A couple of Linux distributions now package
Edit
, including Arch Linux, and Manjaro, so if you use one of those, you can install it properly.
To run
Edit
on Ubuntu you can download the latest binary from the
project GitHub releases page
(be sure to select the correct one for your architecture), extract the package,
cd
into the extracted folder, then launch the binary each time you want to use it:
Download the latest release
(link above)
Extract the archive
(right-click in
Nautilus
>
Extract
)
Open a terminal app
(such as the new
Pytxis
in Ubuntu 25.10
)
Navigate to the extracted folder:
cd /path/to/
Run
Edit
directly:
./edit
To install the unofficial snap build use
App Center
(search ‘msedit’) or run
sudo snap install msedit
from the command line, and use
msedit
to launch it. On my laptop, the snap takes ~5 seconds to open. The official binary is instantaneous. YMMV.
From there, the interface is easy enough to figure out.
Give it a try and let me know what you think!

Edit
Microsoft
Text Editor
44306892.article_summary: Microsoft发布了开源命令行文本编辑器**Edit**，是旧版MS-DOS Editor的现代化重制版，使用Rust编写，旨在提供类似VS Code的界面和输入控制。Edit主要面向Windows用户，因为Windows缺乏内置的CLI文本编辑器，但它也可以在Linux和macOS上运行。Edit功能简洁，主打速度和简易性，支持查找替换、字词换行、多文件编辑等基本功能，但没有语法高亮或配色方案。它采用无模式设计，支持鼠标和键盘操作，易于上手。目前，Edit没有官方的Linux安装程序，但可通过GitHub或Snap安装。未来计划加入更多功能，但核心仍是轻量级文本编辑。

To join the uBlock Origin Lite beta, open the link on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac after you install TestFlight.
Step 1
Get TestFlight
Help developers test beta versions of their apps and App Clips using the

Step 2
View uBlock Origin Lite Beta
**uBO Lite** (uBOL), an efficient [MV3 API-based](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/) content blocker.
uBOL is entirely declarative, meaning there is no need for a permanent uBOL process for the filtering to occur, and CSS/JS injection-based content filtering is [performed reliably](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/scripting/#method-registerContentScripts) by the browser itself rather than by the extension. This means that uBOL itself does not consume CPU/memory resources while content blocking is ongoing -- uBOL's service worker process is required _only_ when you interact with the popup panel or the option pages.
The default ruleset corresponds to at least uBlock Origin's default filterset:
- uBlock Origin's built-in filter lists
- EasyList
- EasyPrivacy
- Peter Lowe’s Ad and tracking server list
You can add more rulesets by visiting the options page -- click the _Cogs_ icon in the popup panel.

Getting started
To test beta versions of apps and App Clips using TestFlight, you’ll need to accept an email or public link invitation from the developer and have a device that you can use to test. You’ll be able to access the builds that the developer makes available to you.

data.title: Behind the scenes: Redpanda Cloud's response to the GCP outage
data.author: eatonphil
data.article_summary: 2025年6月12日，Google Cloud Platform（GCP）由于API管理系统的自动化配额更新引发了全球性宕机，影响了大量互联网服务。然而，Redpanda Cloud的客户未受明显影响，归功于其专门设计的SLA和基于单元（cell-based）的架构。事件过程中，Redpanda Cloud的监控一度处于降级状态，但由于自托管的可观察性数据和堆栈，仍能评估影响。尽管第三方警报服务受影响，Redpanda团队通过其他手段监控系统，提前创建低严重性事件以协调应对潜在问题。在GCP确认问题并实施缓解措施后，Redpanda Cloud未发现客户受负面影响。此次事件展示了复杂系统中的“蝴蝶效应”以及安全和可靠性措施的重要性，如反馈控制、负载削减和回压应用等。尽管警报通知延迟，Redpanda Cloud通过主动联系客户和高错误率处理，成功维持了系统稳定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RedPanda在GCP大规模宕机事件中的表现及其架构设计

不同观点：
• RadiozRadioz：认为文章夸大了RedPanda的成就。虽然他们未受GCP宕机影响，但这主要是因为他们没有使用出问题的服务，且仅依赖第三方报警和监控系统。文章给人一种自夸的感觉，但实际上并没有展示出特别的应急处理或技术亮点，唯一提到的预防措施是超额配置磁盘空间，而这本应是常规操作。

• zzyzxd：批评文章过于冗长且自夸，指出RedPanda的架构并不完美。具体问题包括报警系统不耐用，宕机期间只能人工监控；存储使用超出正常水平且无异常检测和报警。此外，不理解为何要贬低Crowdstrike，认为这是不必要的。

• rybosome：同情GCP当前的处境，指出在大规模宕机事件中，GCP内部可能面临极大的压力和困难，特别是在已经因高可靠性要求而行动受限的情况下。

• diroussel：对文章中关于复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的描述提出异议，认为线性系统也可以是复杂的，并能表现出蝴蝶效应，而不仅仅是非线性系统。

• Peterpanzeri：批评RedPanda的声明，认为“我们的设计恰好没有使用到出问题的服务部分”是一种侥幸心态，希望他们下次能做好准备。

• raverbashing：对文章中将简单的架构原则称为“架构模式”感到有趣，认为这是把 obvious 的事情用复杂的语言表述出来，但认可其观点的正确性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于RedPanda是否真的在此次宕机事件中展现了卓越的技术优势，还是仅仅因为侥幸未受影响。
• 对RedPanda架构设计和报警系统的耐用性、异常检测能力的质疑。
• 对文章中贬低其他公司（如Crowdstrike）的做法表示不解和不满。
• 对复杂系统和蝴蝶效应的技术性讨论，展示了读者对技术概念的不同理解。

Blog
Engineering
Cloud
Behind the scenes: Redpanda Cloudâs response to the GCP outage
What happened, how we handled it, and what we learned during the global GCP outage on June 12th
By
Camilo Aguilar
,
,
,
on
June 20, 2025
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Copy
link
CopIED!
On Jun 12th, 2025, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experienced an unfortunate global outage triggered by an automated quota update to their API management system.Â
What was a major outage for a large part of the internet was just another normal day for
Redpanda Cloud
customers. While GCP dealt with the widespread disruption that impacted many critical services, Redpanda Cloud clusters in GCP remained stable, thanks to being purposely designed for the
SLA we offer
, along with a
cell-based architecture
that we also made a
product principle
. But behind the scenes, it was far from quiet.
This post provides a brief timeline of events from our own experience, our response, previously untold details about Redpanda Cloud, and closing thoughts on safety and reliability practices in our industry.
Why do incidents like this happen
Modern computer systems are complex systems âÂ and complex systems are characterized by their non-linear nature, which means that observed changes in an output
are not
proportional to the change in the input. This concept is also known in chaos theory as the
butterfly effect
, or in systems thinking, with the expression, âThe whole is greater than the sum of its partsâ.Â
When this mathematical fact is acknowledged, safety and reliabiilty measures are put in place, such as closing feedback control loops, phasing change rollouts, shedding load, applying backpressure, randomizing retries, and defining incident response processes, among others.
GCPâs seemingly innocuous automated quota update triggered a
butterfly effect
that no human could have predicted, affecting several companies âÂ some known for their impressive engineering culture and considered internet pillars for their long-standing availability record.
The timeline
18:41:00 UTC
Our Google Cloud Technical Account Manager (TAM) notified us about the outage:
18:42:00 UTC
We began to assess the impact on our Redpanda Cloud GCP customers, including whether we had received any support tickets.Â
18:43:00 UTC
We noticed our monitoring was running in a degraded state. Despite self-hosting our observability data and stack, we still use a third-party provider for dashboarding and alerting needs. This provider was partially affected. We could still monitor metrics, but we were not getting alert notifications.Â
We deemed the loss of alert notifications not critical since we were still able to assess the impact through other means, such as querying our self-managed metrics and logging stack.
19:08:00 UTC
At this point, it was clear that multiple GCP services were experiencing a global outage, despite not having received support tickets from our customers or being paged by Redpanda Cloud alerts. So, in preparation for the worst, we preemptively created a low-severity incident to coordinate the response to multiple
potential
incidents.
19:23:00 UTC
We were notified by the vendor we use for managing cloud marketplaces that they were having issues. They were affected by the
Cloudflare outage
, which we later learned was connected to the GCP outage. Having this service degraded was not critical to us, so we put it on the waiting list.
19:41:00 UTC
Google identified the triggering cause and applied mitigations. At this point, there was no evidence that Redpanda Cloud customers were being negatively impacted.
20:26:00 UTC
We began receiving delayed alert notifications, mostly related to an increase in tiered storage errors, which is not Redpandaâs primary storage. 44338089.article_summary: 2025年6月12日，Google Cloud Platform（GCP）由于API管理系统的自动化配额更新引发了全球性宕机，影响了大量互联网服务。然而，Redpanda Cloud的客户未受明显影响，归功于其专门设计的SLA和基于单元（cell-based）的架构。事件过程中，Redpanda Cloud的监控一度处于降级状态，但由于自托管的可观察性数据和堆栈，仍能评估影响。尽管第三方警报服务受影响，Redpanda团队通过其他手段监控系统，提前创建低严重性事件以协调应对潜在问题。在GCP确认问题并实施缓解措施后，Redpanda Cloud未发现客户受负面影响。此次事件展示了复杂系统中的“蝴蝶效应”以及安全和可靠性措施的重要性，如反馈控制、负载削减和回压应用等。尽管警报通知延迟，Redpanda Cloud通过主动联系客户和高错误率处理，成功维持了系统稳定。

data.title: Fundamental Problems of Lisp, the Cons Cell (2024)
data.author: gudzpoz
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了LISP语言中的一个基本问题：cons单元用于构建列表的局限性。LISP的核心是基于函数式编程和列表操作，但其列表结构依赖于硬件概念的cons单元，导致每个列表节点只能包含两个元素。若要构建更长的列表，必须嵌套cons单元并采用特殊解释方式，称为“适当列表”。这种设计限制了列表处理的发展，使得操作复杂且不统一。文章建议通过标准化适当列表和隐藏低级cons操作来改进LISP。同时，作者批评了cons及其相关函数（如car、cdr等）导致代码不一致和复杂性，并以假设语言gisp中的三元单元fons为例，说明了类似问题。最后，文章探讨了LISP的cons问题为何未被解决，归因于历史和技术限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp中的cons细胞和其作为基础数据结构的角色

不同观点：
• noosphr认为Lisp的核心不是函数式编程，而是对抽象语法树的直接操作。同时，嵌套列表的深度通常较浅，复杂的操作很少见。Lisp的强大在于实现领域特定语言（DSL），如Emacs的elisp实现。
• lisper强调cons细胞作为原始数据结构的价值，指出其与C语言中指针操作的区别。认为cons细胞的问题在于不当的抽象使用，而非其本身有问题。
• DonaldFisk认为cons细胞是Lisp不可或缺的一部分，类似于Smalltalk中的对象和APL中的数组。其他语言也有类似的数据结构，Lisp程序员普遍认为cons细胞和列表非常有用。
• alphazard指出cons细胞的间接机制与其连接机制混淆的问题，建议将值的组合与存储分开处理，以实现更高效的内存使用。
• behnamoh提到Janet这个Lisp方言，虽然文档不足，但其编译成小二进制文件和支持图像的特点令人喜爱。
• gudzpoz分享了在为Lisp方言编写JIT运行时的经验，认为cons风格的链表在性能上难以与数组竞争，但正在尝试通过JIT优化来改进。
• smarks回顾了Xah Lee多年来对cons细胞的批评，认为这是一个老生常谈的问题，并引用了历史讨论中其他人的观点。
• Jtsummers通过引用LISP I手册，解释cons、car和cdr是用于创建和操作S表达式的原始工具，而非仅限于列表操作，强调其历史和合理性。
• dragontamer简要说明cons细胞作为基础数据结构的强大和灵活性，但也指出高性能现代编程中数组的重要性。
• chubot提到Clojure中cons细胞使用较少，因为其基于不可变的地图和向量。
• kazinator在TXR Lisp中展示了car/cdr的扩展使用，通过定义新结构和方法来实现更多功能。

补充讨论：
• 对Xah Lee的批评：多个评论者提到Xah Lee对cons细胞的批评，并对其观点提出质疑，认为其可能缺乏深入理解。
• 历史背景：smarks和Jtsummers都提到了Lisp的历史文档和早期讨论，提供了对cons细胞历史和设计的更深理解。
• 性能问题：gudzpoz和dragontamer都提到了cons细胞在现代硬件上的性能问题，并讨论了可能的优化方法。

争议焦点：
• cons细胞的抽象和使用是否恰当，以及其在现代编程需求下的性能和实用性。

44310996.article_content:
Fundamental Problems of LISP, the Cons Cell
By Xah Lee. Date:
2024-07-02
.
(this essay is originally written around 2008)
The Cons Business
The other fundamental problem in the language is its cons cells as its list construction primitive.
Lisp at core is based on functional programing on lists.
This is a powerful paradigm.
However, for historical reasons, lisp's list is based on the hardware concept of âconsâ cell.
From a mathematical, functional, API point of view, what this means is that lisp's âlistâ is limited to a max of 2 elements.
If you want a longer list, you must nest it and interpret it in a special way.
(i.e.
effectively creating a mini-protocol, known as âproper listâ.)
The cons fundamentally crippled the development of list processing.
Lisp being historically based the cons for about 4 decades. The cons and the associated {car cdr cadr caadr caddr caaar cdddr â¦} are fundamentally rooted in the lisp langs, is thus not something that can be easily mended. This is unfortunate. However, this situation could be improved.  By, for example:
Create a standard that all list data structures must be proper lists. (this would also mean re-implement association lists to be based on proper lists)
Expose only higher-level list manipulation functions (i.e. interfaces to cons) in all new literature.
Even mark cons related constructs as obsolete.
One of the myth that is quickly injected into budding lispers, is that cons is powerful. It is powerful in the sense assembly lang is powerful.
Lisp's cons is perhaps the greatest fuck up in the history of computer languages.
Racket Lisp described the cons problem well:
Racket Doc on Lisp Cons Problem
For some concrete examples of problems caused by the cons, see:
Guy Steele Says: Don't Iterate, Recurse, and Get rid of lisp cons!
Why Lisp Not Have a Generic Copy-List Function?
Lisp List Problem
Frequently Asked Questions
If you don't like cons, lisp has arrays and hashmaps, too.
Suppose there's a lang called gisp.
In gisp, there's cons but also fons.
Fons is just like cons except it has 3 cells with 3 accessors: car, cbr, cdr.
Now, gisp is a old lang, the fons are deeply rooted in the lang.
Every some 100 lines of code you'll see a use of fons with its extra accessor cbr, or any one of the cbaar, cdabr, cbbar, cbbbar, etc.
You got annoyed by this.
You complain that fons is bad.
But then some gisp fanatics retorts: âIf you don't like fons, gisp has cons, too!â.
You see, by âhaving something tooâ, does not solve the problem of pollution.
I like the cons concept. Even in functional languages like Haskell it is popular, for example, when matching in the form of (x:xs), which is the same like car/cdr in Lisp.
Languages that have a list data type implemented as linked list, with First, Rest accessors, do not expose it as API in the same way lisp does with explicit cons.
Lisp's cons forces programer to think of list in a low-level nested of 2-item construction, with explicit functions like âcddrâ, âcadaarâ etc, and even a special notation â(A .
B)â.
This hinders the development tree functions.
For example, one might write a function that extracts the leafs of a binary tree.
But due to cons, there is no single data structure to implement a binary tree.
You can have the whole structure made of cons, or cons only for ending branches, or whole structure made of âproper listâ.
Consequently, what's considered a leaf depends on your implementation, and the code to traverse the tree also depends on how you used cons.
Worse, any proper list can have improper list as elements.
So, you can have a list of cons, or cons of lists, cons of cons, list of lists, or any mix.
The overall effect of the cons is that it prevents lisp to have a uniform high level treatment of lists, with the result that development of functions that work on tree are inconsistent and few.
2009-07-21 Addendum : there was actually a lang with âfonsâ of 3 cells. {Haines, E.
C., The TREET List Processing Language.
M.S.
Thesis, MIT, Cambridge, Mass., August 1964.
Also SR-133, The MITRE Corporation, Bedford, Mass., April 1965.} Thanks to
Richard Fateman
for alerting me to this.
Why Lisp's Cons Problem Never Got Fixed?
Now, a little speculation.
We might wonder, why lisp has the cons problem and was never addressed in Common Lisp or Scheme Lisp?
Historical Necessity
I guess at the time, 1960s and 1970s, the very fact that you could have a concept like a list in a lang and manipulate it as a unit, is a very advanced concept.
The list, being built up by hardware cons, is just something that is necessary for implementation for practical considerations.
(think for a moment what computers are like in the 1960s.)
Having data as a single manipulable object (list) didn't really become popular until the 1990s.
(notably due to Perl) And today, it is THE most important feature of high-level languages.
(e.g. Perl Python Ruby PHP JavaScript)
Deep Nesting is Rare

data.title: Record DDoS pummels site with once-unimaginable 7.3Tbps of junk traffic
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了一次创纪录的DDoS攻击，其流量达到7.3Tbps，针对Cloudflare的一名客户。攻击者使用了“地毯式轰炸”策略，向单个IP地址的多个端口发送大量垃圾数据，其中大部分通过UDP协议传输。UDP洪水攻击通过发送高量数据包使目标服务器过载。此外，攻击还利用了反射攻击技术，借助中间服务器放大攻击效果。此次攻击还涉及Mirai僵尸网络，由被入侵的物联网设备组成。DDoS攻击规模在过去几十年中不断增大，显示出网络安全面临的持续威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare宣称阻止大规模网络攻击的可信度及技术细节

不同观点：

• ksec则关注用户体验问题，特别是当Cloudflare的验证码（captcha）不工作时，用户（尤其是在特定设备和浏览器上）该如何应对，提出了替代方案的需求。
• esafak提出了关于攻击者身份和动机的问题，质疑谁在发动攻击以及他们的目的。
• encom强烈质疑Cloudflare的可信度，认为这篇文章像是一篇赞助广告，缺乏可验证的细节，并对Ars Technica发布这样的内容表示失望。

补充讨论：
• ChrisArchitect提到在另一个讨论平台（Hacker News）上有重复的讨论，并提供了链接供参考。
• balanc质疑Cloudflare是否有动机夸大其成功阻止的攻击规模，指出Cloudflare可能有经济利益驱动，并预先反驳了可能的反驳意见。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare宣称阻止的攻击规模是否真实，是否存在夸大其词的情况。
• 对Cloudflare的整体可信度及媒体报道的真实性存在广泛质疑。

Large-scale attacks designed to bring down Internet services by sending them more traffic than they can process keep getting bigger, with the largest one yet, measured at 7.3 terabits per second, being reported Friday by Internet security and performance provider Cloudflare.
The 7.3Tbps attack amounted to 37.4 terabytes of junk traffic that hit the target in just 45 seconds. That's an almost incomprehensible amount of data, equivalent to more than 9,300 full-length HD movies or 7,500 hours of HD streaming content in well under a minute.
Indiscriminate target bombing
Cloudflare
said
the attackers “carpet bombed” an average of nearly 22,000 destination ports of a single IP address belonging to the target, identified only as a Cloudflare customer. A total of 34,500 ports were targeted, indicating the thoroughness and well-engineered nature of the attack.
The vast majority of the attack was delivered in the form of User Datagram Protocol packets. Legitimate UDP-based transmissions are used in especially time-sensitive communications, such as those for video playback, gaming applications, and DNS lookups. It speeds up communications by not formally establishing a connection before data is transferred. Unlike the more common Transmission Control Protocol, UDP doesn't wait for a connection between two computers to be established through a handshake and doesn't check whether data is properly received by the other party. Instead, it immediately sends data from one machine to another.
UDP flood attacks send extremely high volumes of packets to random or specific ports on the target IP. Such floods can saturate the target’s Internet link or overwhelm internal resources with more packets than they can handle.
Since UDP doesn't require a handshake, attackers can use it to flood a targeted server with torrents of traffic without first obtaining the server's permission to begin the transmission. UDP floods typically send large numbers of datagrams to multiple ports on the target system. The target system, in turn, must send an equal number of data packets back to indicate the ports aren't reachable. Eventually, the target system buckles under the strain, resulting in legitimate traffic being denied.
A much smaller portion of the attack, measured at just 0.004 percent, was delivered as reflection attacks. Reflection attacks direct malicious traffic to one or more third-party intermediaries, such as Network Time Protocol services for syncing server clocks. The attacker spoofs the sender IP of the malicious packets to give the appearance they’re being delivered by the final target. When the third party sends a response, it's delivered to the target rather than the destination of the original source of the traffic.
Reflection attacks provide multiple benefits to attackers. For one, such attacks cause the DDoS to be delivered from a wide variety of destinations. That makes it harder for targets to defend against the onslaught. Additionally, by choosing intermediary servers known to generate responses that are in some cases thousands of times bigger than the originating request, attackers can magnify the firepower available to them by a thousandfold or more. Cloudflare and other players routinely advise server administrators to lock down servers to prevent them from responding to spoofed packets, but inevitably, many don't heed the advice.
Cloudflare said the record DDoS exploited various reflection or amplification vectors, including the previously mentioned Network Time Protocol; the Quote of the Day Protocol, which listens on UDP port 17 and responds with a short quote or message; the Echo Protocol, which responds with the same data it receives; and Portmapper services used identify resources available to applications connecting through the Remote Procedure Call.
Cloudflare said the attack was also delivered through one or more Mirai-based botnets. Such botnets are typically made up of home and small office routers, web cameras, and other Internet of Things devices that have been compromised.
DDoS sizes have continued a steady climb over the past three decades. In
March
, Nokia reported that a botnet dubbed Eleven11bot delivered a DOS with a peak of 6.5Tbps. In May, KrebsonSecurity
said
it came under a DDos that peaked at 6.3Tbps.

44337225.article_summary: 文章主要报道了一次创纪录的DDoS攻击，其流量达到7.3Tbps，针对Cloudflare的一名客户。攻击者使用了“地毯式轰炸”策略，向单个IP地址的多个端口发送大量垃圾数据，其中大部分通过UDP协议传输。UDP洪水攻击通过发送高量数据包使目标服务器过载。此外，攻击还利用了反射攻击技术，借助中间服务器放大攻击效果。此次攻击还涉及Mirai僵尸网络，由被入侵的物联网设备组成。DDoS攻击规模在过去几十年中不断增大，显示出网络安全面临的持续威胁。

不同观点：

• ksec则关注用户体验问题，特别是当Cloudflare的验证码（captcha）不工作时，用户（尤其是在特定设备和浏览器上）该如何应对，提出了替代方案的需求。
• esafak提出了关于攻击者身份和动机的问题，质疑谁在发动攻击以及他们的目的。
• encom强烈质疑Cloudflare的可信度，认为这篇文章像是一篇赞助广告，缺乏可验证的细节，并对Ars Technica发布这样的内容表示失望。

补充讨论：

data.author: dlwh
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了利用大型语言模型（LLM）自动化将C语言程序移植到Rust的潜力，特别是通过模糊测试和拓扑排序构建移植策略的有效性。作者反思了LLM生成代码的趋势，预测未来计算机将生成大部分代码，从而改变库维护和API管理的方式。LLM可以帮助解决API不一致问题，甚至可以自动迁移到新版本，从而简化大规模重构。文章还以TensorFlow为例，说明维护大型技术债务项目所面临的挑战，并提出通过LLM降低复杂重构成本的可能性。这为未来代码维护和库改进提供了新的思路。

44307275.article_content:
The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Fuzzing for Porting Programs
A simple strategy of having LLMs write fuzz tests and build up a port in topological order seems effective at automating porting from C to Rust.
Agents are starting to produce more and more code
A week or 2 back, I was reflecting on some code Claude had generated for me and
I had a sort of moment of clarity. "Clarity" might be overstating it; more
like the type of thought you have in the shower or after a few beers. Anyway.
The thought was: LLMs produce more and more code, and they'll eventually be
producing more code than people. We can imagine at some point we're going to
fork from mostly people writing code to mostly computers. What does this mean
for how we're going to treat our libraries and code maintenance in the future?
LLMs make it easier to deal with API issues or inconsistencies, they're dealing
with it, not us. Will this continue, leaving us with a
The
Princess and the Pea
situation where we deal with piles of leaking
abstractions? Or will we use LLMs to radically change our APIs when needed - will
things get cleaner and better and faster as we go?
LLMs open up the door to performing radical updates that we'd
never really consider in the past. We can port our libraries from one language
to another. We can change our APIs to fix issues, and give downstream users an
LLM prompt to migrate over to the new version automatically, instead of
rewriting their code themselves. We can make massive internal refactorings.
These are types of tasks that in the past,
rightly
, a senior engineer would
reject in a project until its the last possibly option. Breaking customers
almost never pays off, and its hard to justify refactoring on a "maintenance
mode" project.
But if its more about finding the right prompt and letting an
LLM do the work, maybe that changes our decision process.
Maintaining big important libraries is no fun
I used to work on
TensorFlow
. (TensorFlow is a system to develop
gradient based models, like PyTorch. It's not used so much anymore outside of
Google.) Now TensorFlow had some design flaws in the core language, and a
botched version 1 -> version 2 migration didn't help matters too much. But as a
maintainer, the biggest issue was the enormous technical debt. It suffered from
a sort of "career advancement syndrome"
I sadly missed this period and only was around for the aftermath where we had to deal with the cruft.
: TensorFlow was popular and you got credit for
contributing to it, so there was a huge incentive to add some feature as quickly
as you could and then get away.
As a result of a few years of this style of development, a huge surface of
Python code had been cobbled together on top of the C++ core. The complexity
only spiraled over time: engineers came into the project and needed to get
something done. Increasingly the easiest thing to do was to add some Python global or
context manager, shove something in it, then grab it later. Do this over and
over and eventually it becomes impossibly to figure out what's happening. It
also ended up being incredibly slow. It would take 10s of minutes to build some
graphs (TensorFlow's equivalent of a program).
As a result of this over time TensorFlow became harder and harder to maintain,
much less evolve
It was also hard to keep good engineers working on the project. If
you're a good engineer, other teams want you and you could choose to work on
less crufty, more exciting projects like
Jax
or
XLA
, or you know, Ads.
. One idea we discussed internally to try to fix this was
porting the Python code, bit by bit, into a more comprehensible C++ layer, and
then re-exporting it via PyBind. At first you'd still call everything through
the Python interface, but as you ported code over, you could start to use the
internal C++ interfaces more and more, getting faster and more stable as you
went. This would incrementally improve the performance and consistency of the
system, or that was the hope.
But it would have been an enormous effort to do this all. Each time you tried to
port a module you'd reveal subtle errors or assumptions that you'd need to debug
and revisit, update users etc. Given our staffing, we couldn't really justify
the time versus the real work of making sure Ads didn't break.
Even though TensorFlow was moving to maintenance mode, if we could have made
this type of change it would have improved the maintainer and users' experience
for the years we need to keep the lights on. But because the cleanup was thorny
and slow, we just couldn't justify the cost.
This is by no means limited to TensorFlow. If you're working on something like
libexpat
its hard to justify
refactoring your code or rewriting it in Rust, no matter how potentially useful
it would be, when you've got this at the top of your page:
But what if we could make this type of refactoring much, much cheaper?

主要讨论点：欧洲是否应减少对美国技术和政治支持的依赖，以及微软在此次事件中的角色和责任。

不同观点：
• bigtones和gentle认为，此次事件为欧洲提供了明确的证据，表明欧洲应减少对美国的依赖，发展自己的技术和基础设施，以保护自身利益。bigtones还以澳大利亚的立场为例，认为澳大利亚也应该这样做。

• NewJazz和decide1000对微软的反应表示不满。NewJazz批评微软没有抵抗或上诉美国的命令，显示其软弱和顺从。decide1000则认为，微软的行动破坏了欧美之间长期以来的关系，欧洲人将加速与美国的分离。

• nickdothutton提到，欧洲曾有计划建立自己的技术和基础设施，但未付诸实施。这表明欧洲有想法但缺乏行动力。

• creatonez将微软的行为与历史上其他科技公司参与战争罪行的例子相提并论，认为微软在当前的国际冲突中扮演了不光彩的角色。

• dudeinjapan分享了个人经历，提到微软曾在未警告的情况下暂停其电子邮件账户，认为此次事件属于更大、更险恶模式的一部分。

• yahoozoo将事件归因于以色列，暗示以色列在背后的影响。

data.title: Astronomers locate universe's 'missing' matter in the largest cosmic structures
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 天文学家发现了一条巨大的炽热气体丝状结构，连接四个星系团，长达2300万光年，质量为银河系的10倍。这一发现解释了宇宙中长期缺失的“普通物质”位置，这些物质以原子形式存在，构成了星星、行星等。此前，宇宙模型预测这些缺失的物质存在于连接密集星系团的丝状气体中，但因其暗淡且被其他光源掩盖，难以观测。通过XMM-Newton和Suzaku太空望远镜，天文学家首次清晰观测到这一结构，验证了宇宙模型的准确性，并有助于理解宇宙网（Cosmic Web）及宇宙大规模结构的形成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙中“失踪气体”（missing baryons）问题以及其与暗物质理论的关系。

不同观点：
• [mosesbp的观点] 认为该研究仅分析了相对宇宙整体较小区域内的星系间气体（特别是WHIM），并指出作者自己也承认需要更多高质量的数据才能得出更确凿的结论。同时提到失踪气体问题是一个长期存在的难题，并引用多篇文献说明近年来有研究利用快速射电暴（Fast Radio Burst）数据尝试解决该问题，暗示气体存在于WHIM中可能是失踪气体的合理解释。
  
• [exegete的观点] 提出疑问，是否这意味着理论上的暗物质数量减少，因为暗物质的存在是为了解释观测到的引力效应，这些效应表明宇宙中应该存在比我们实际观测到的更多物质。这暗示了对失踪气体的解释可能会影响到暗物质理论的有效性。

补充讨论：
• [失踪气体的背景] mosesbp指出失踪气体问题主要集中在宇宙相对“近期”的历史中，并提到已有文献讨论了这一问题，强调了失踪气体和存在于星系间的气体（WHIM）之间的关联。
  
• [暗物质与失踪气体的关系] exegete的评论引发了关于失踪气体和暗物质之间关系的讨论。暗物质被认为是为了解释观测到的引力效应而假设的存在，而失踪气体问题则涉及普通物质的分布，二者虽然都涉及宇宙中的物质不足问题，但本质上属于不同的问题领域。

争议焦点：失踪气体的发现是否会减少对暗物质的需求，或二者是否存在相互影响。这涉及到宇宙学中对不同形式物质的理解和解释。

44338001.article_content:
An illustration of the cosmic web where the universe's missing matter was discovered
(Image credit: ESA/XMM-Newton and ISAS/JAXA.)
Astronomers have discovered a vast tendril of hot gas linking four galaxy clusters and stretching out for 23 million light-years, 230 times the length of our galaxy. With 10 times the mass of the Milky Way, this filamentary structure accounts for much of the universe's "missing matter," the search for which has baffled scientists for decades.
This "missing matter"
doesn't
refer to
dark matter
, the mysterious stuff that remains effectively invisible because it doesn't interact with light (sadly, that remains an ongoing puzzle). Instead, it is "ordinary matter" made up of atoms, composed of
electrons
,
protons
, and
neutrons
(collectively called
baryons
) which make up stars, planets, moons, and our bodies.
For decades, our best models of the universe have suggested that a third of the baryonic matter that should be out there in the cosmos is missing. This discovery of that missing matter suggests our best models of the universe were right all along. It could also reveal more about the "
Cosmic Web,
" the vast structure along which entire galaxies grew and gathered during the earlier epochs of our
13.8 billion-year-old universe.
The aforementioned models of the cosmos, including the
standard model of cosmology
, have long posited the idea that the missing baryonic matter of the universe is locked up in vast filaments of gas stretching between the densest pockets of space.

Though astronomers have seen these filaments before, the fact that they are faint has meant that their light has been washed out by other sources like galaxies and
supermassive black hole
-powered
quasars
. That means the characteristics of these filaments have remained elusive.
But now, a team of astronomers has for the first time been able to determine the properties of one of these filaments, which links four galactic clusters in the local universe. These four clusters are all part of the
Shapley Supercluster
, a gathering of over 8,000 galaxies forming one of the most massive structures in the nearby cosmos.
"For the first time, our results closely match what we see in our leading model of the cosmos – something that's not happened before," team leader Konstantinos Migkas of Leiden Observatory in the Netherlands said in a statement. "It seems that the simulations were right all along."
Missing matter is hot stuff
The newly observed filament isn't just extraordinary in terms of its mass and size; it also has a temperature of a staggering 18 million degrees Fahrenheit (10 million degrees Celsius). That's around 1,800 times hotter than the
surface of the sun.

While Suzaku, a
Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
(JAXA) satellite, mapped X-ray light over a vast region of space, the
European Space Agency
(ESA) operated XMM-Newton zoomed in of X-ray points from supermassive black holes studded within the filament, "contaminating" it.
"Thanks to XMM-Newton, we could identify and remove these cosmic contaminants, so we knew we were looking at the gas in the filament and nothing else," team member and University of Bonn researcher Florian Pacaud said. "Our approach was really successful, and reveals that the filament is exactly as we'd expect from our best
large-scale simulations of the universe
."
The team then combined these X-ray observations with optical data from a plethora of other telescopes.
The core of the Shapley Supercluster, the largest cosmic structure in the local universe.
(Image credit: ESA & Planck Collaboration / Rosat/ Digitised Sky Survey)
Revealing this hitherto undiscovered tendril of hot matter connecting galaxy clusters has the potential to aid scientists' understanding of these extreme structures and how they are connected across
vast cosmic distances.
This could, in turn, aid our understanding of the Cosmic Web, filaments of matter that acted as a cosmic scaffold helping the universe to assemble in it
44338001.article_summary: 天文学家发现了一条巨大的炽热气体丝状结构，连接四个星系团，长达2300万光年，质量为银河系的10倍。这一发现解释了宇宙中长期缺失的“普通物质”位置，这些物质以原子形式存在，构成了星星、行星等。此前，宇宙模型预测这些缺失的物质存在于连接密集星系团的丝状气体中，但因其暗淡且被其他光源掩盖，难以观测。通过XMM-Newton和Suzaku太空望远镜，天文学家首次清晰观测到这一结构，验证了宇宙模型的准确性，并有助于理解宇宙网（Cosmic Web）及宇宙大规模结构的形成。
44338001.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙中“失踪气体”（missing baryons）问题以及其与暗物质理论的关系。

不同观点：
• [mosesbp的观点] 认为该研究仅分析了相对宇宙整体较小区域内的星系间气体（特别是WHIM），并指出作者自己也承认需要更多高质量的数据才能得出更确凿的结论。同时提到失踪气体问题是一个长期存在的难题，并引用多篇文献说明近年来有研究利用快速射电暴（Fast Radio Burst）数据尝试解决该问题，暗示气体存在于WHIM中可能是失踪气体的合理解释。
  
• [exegete的观点] 提出疑问，是否这意味着理论上的暗物质数量减少，因为暗物质的存在是为了解释观测到的引力效应，这些效应表明宇宙中应该存在比我们实际观测到的更多物质。这暗示了对失踪气体的解释可能会影响到暗物质理论的有效性。

补充讨论：
• [失踪气体的背景] mosesbp指出失踪气体问题主要集中在宇宙相对“近期”的历史中，并提到已有文献讨论了这一问题，强调了失踪气体和存在于星系间的气体（WHIM）之间的关联。
  
• [暗物质与失踪气体的关系] exegete的评论引发了关于失踪气体和暗物质之间关系的讨论。暗物质被认为是为了解释观测到的引力效应而假设的存在，而失踪气体问题则涉及普通物质的分布，二者虽然都涉及宇宙中的物质不足问题，但本质上属于不同的问题领域。

争议焦点：失踪气体的发现是否会减少对暗物质的需求，或二者是否存在相互影响。这涉及到宇宙学中对不同形式物质的理解和解释。

data.title: MCP Specification – version 2025-06-18 changes
data.author: owebmaster
data.article_summary:
《Model Context Protocol》2025-06-18版更新文档总结了自2025-03-26版以来的主要变更：

**主要变更**：
1. 移除对JSON-RPC批处理的支持(PR #416)。
2. 增加对结构化工具输出的支持(PR #371)。
3. 将MCP服务器分类为OAuth资源服务器，并增加受保护资源元数据以发现相应的授权服务器(PR #338)。
4. 要求MCP客户端实现RFC 8707中的资源指示器，以防止恶意服务器获取访问令牌(PR #734)。
5. 澄清授权规范中的安全考虑和最佳实践，并新增安全最佳实践页面。
6. 增加对引出的支持，允许服务器在交互过程中请求用户额外信息(PR #382)。
7. 增加对工具调用结果中资源链接的支持(PR #603)。
8. 要求通过HTTP请求中的MCP-Protocol-Version头指定协商的协议版本(PR #548)。
9. 将生命周期操作中的“应”改为“必须”。

**其他模式变更**：
1. 向其他接口类型添加_meta字段并指定其正确使用(PR #710)。
2. 向CompletionRequest添加context字段，允许完成请求包含先前解析的变量(PR #598)。
3. 增加title字段作为人性化显示名称，使name可作为编程标识符使用(PR #663)。

完整变更日志见GitHub。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Machine Control Protocol）的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• neya：认为MCP在编写后端软件时增加了不必要的复杂性。每个API一个服务器并不合理，尤其在Elixir中，建议使用模块而不是独立的服务器来实现API功能。
• dend：对MCP服务器授权路径的简化表示欢迎，并对MCP社区和Anthropic的贡献表示感谢。
• elliotbnvl：对核心规范使用TypeScript而不是OpenAPI感到意外，但认为也有其合理性。
• eadmund：虽然认为MCP复杂且不必要，但赞赏其批处理功能，可以一次性执行多个任务。
• swalsh：强调MCP在自动化服务器任务中的优势，但也指出在认证管理上的不便。
• disintegrator：赞赏引入WWW-Authenticate挑战，认为这使得MCP服务器能够更清晰地处理认证流程。
• gotts：对MCP规范的快速改进表示高兴，每次新版本发布都能解决一些集成问题。

补充讨论：
• martinald：分享了使用MCP的经验和问题，包括C# SDK的认证问题、日志缺失以及处理长时间任务的困难，特别是如何有效处理PDF文件和长时间运行的任务。
• Aeolun：对规范更改只需一次批准即可合并表示调侃。
• whazor：建议引入资源更新/删除的审批工作流，以便MCP服务器可以有OAuth链接来批准特定步骤。
• jjfoooo4：质疑MCP的实际解决能力，认为对于本地程序和服务器程序，RPC是更好的选择，MCP增加了不必要的中间件和安全漏洞。
• surfingdino：对LLM的结构化输出表示怀疑，认为这是一个需要大量防御性编程的领域。
• fennecfoxy：关注MCP的安全问题，如恶意服务器、提示注入和数据窃取。
• dgellow：计划在周末更新其MCP OAuth代理。
• freed0mdox：认为MCP缺乏合理的异步回调方式，以便使用自定义提示和操作结果查询模型。

争议焦点：
• MCP是否引入了不必要的复杂性，特别是在后端架构中。
• MCP在安全性和日志记录方面的不足。
• MCP在处理长时间任务和异步操作方面的局限性。

总的来说，讨论围绕MCP的实用性、复杂性、安全性和改进空间展开，不同用户根据自身经验和需求对MCP持不同看法。

At Weave, we’re building the best software for the best engineering teams to move faster, and we want to hire exceptional engineers to help us do so.
We are a well-funded startup, backed by top investors, growing rapidly and currently profitable.
You'll be working directly with me (Andrew), the CTO. Before I was CTO of Weave I was the founding engineer at Causal, and I want to give you all the support and growth opportunities in this role that I got when I went through it.
You’ll also be working directly with Adam, the CEO. Adam runs sales at Weave, and before that worked as a sales executive at a few different high growth startups.
Must haves
You are a good fit for Weave if you are a
formidable
engineer. This means you stop at nothing to accomplish your goal. We don't care much about your current skills or even what you've done before; we care that you will be able to do anything you set your mind to.
You must also be pragmatic. Weave is a startup so something is always on fire. You need to know when to let little fires burn and when to break out the extinguisher.
You must be a very good engineer who's committed to becoming a great engineer. The slope is more important than the Y-intercept.
You must be empathetic. We're building products for other people, so you need to be able to understand how other people think and why.
You must care about helping other software engineering teams be great. If that's not an exciting mission for you, it will be hard to stay motivated through the inevitable highs and lows.
You must be an excellent communicator. You’ll be working on a product that’s communicating with millions of engineers and leaders, so you need to be clear.
Finally you must be gritty. You should be accustomed to picking the hard option and pushing through it.
Nice to haves
(Please feel free to apply even if some or all of these don't apply to you!)
Our tech stack is React + TypeScript on the frontend, Go on the backend, and Python for ML. Experience with any of those three languages is a bonus.
If you've already done lots of thinking about engineering productivity and how to improve it, that's great and we want to hear about it!
We hope your design sensibilities are passable.

As Weave’s founding AI engineer, your job is to build AI to understand and improve the work that software engineers do. You’ll be building our processes and standards as you go to make building every incremental feature easier. Your goal will be to delight customers with intelligence that makes their job 10x easier.

data.title: Tell HN: Beware confidentiality agreements that act as lifetime non competes
data.author: throwarayes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非竞争协议（Non-compete agreements）及其在不同国家和地区的有效性、合理性和影响。

不同观点：
• **中国法律对非竞争协议的保护**：[tianqi]指出，根据中国法律，公司必须按月支付员工在职时月收入的30%作为补偿，否则非竞争协议自动失效。这种机制被认为能有效保护员工的权益。

• **美国非竞争协议的滥用**：[timoth3y]认为，美国雇主滥用非竞争协议，甚至让时薪20美元以下的工人签署，尽管这些工人并没有接触到商业机密，协议只是为了削弱工人的谈判能力。

• **州际法律差异与经济影响**：[kirubakaran]提到，华盛顿等州为了“商业友好”而执行非竞争协议，而加利福尼亚禁止非竞争协议，其GDP却是全球第四大，暗示非竞争协议未必有利于经济发展。

• **合同条款的实际可执行性**：[tgsovlerkhgsel]提醒不要被复杂的合同条款吓倒，建议在有疑问时咨询律师。有些条款看似吓人，但实际上无法执行。

• **加州的法律立场**：[wbl]指出，加州法院对非竞争协议的过度扩张持否定态度，依据是成文法和判例法对商业秘密的保护规定。

• **工会对非竞争协议的限制**：[matsemann]分享其国家通过工会禁止广泛的非竞争协议，要求协议必须具体、期限最长一年，且公司需支付员工在其不能工作期间的薪水。

• **合同条款的合理性**：[gwbas1c]提到曾拒绝一份包含复杂非竞争条款的工作，认为这些条款不合理且难以理解。

• **非竞争条款在不同国家的合法性**：[sim7c00]指出，在其国家，任何阻止员工找工作的合同条款基本无效，法院不会支持。

• **面对不合理条款的选择**：[dakiol]指出，在一些国家，非竞争条款是非法的，求职者可以选择要求删除条款或冒险签署但不予理会。

data.title: Airpass – easily overcome WiFi time limits
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: Airpass for Mac是一款可以更改设备MAC地址的工具。当你连接到WiFi网络时，网络会记录你的MAC地址，即使使用不同凭据再次登录，系统仍可能识别出同一设备并限制使用。通过使用Airpass更改MAC地址，WiFi网络将无法识别你的设备，从而绕过限制，让你继续正常使用网络。该工具由Tiago Alves在旅行中开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过修改MAC地址实现网络访问控制或隐私保护的各种方法及工具

不同观点：
• classichasclass和purplehat_提供了在MacOS和Linux上通过命令行修改MAC地址的具体方法。classichasclass使用`sudo`命令结合`airport`和`ifconfig`工具，而purplehat_则提出了在Linux上生成随机MAC地址的脚本，并指出某些命令可能生成无效的MAC地址。
• ammar2讨论了现代操作系统（如MacOS和Android）内置的MAC地址随机化功能，并提供了官方文档链接。他还提到了Windows上的相关设置，强调了各系统中修改MAC地址的简便性。
• vachina分享了一个实际案例，通过在Linux上绑定多个虚拟网卡来绕过网络带宽限制，展示了MAC地址修改在实际场景中的应用。
• johnebgd提到使用MAC地址白名单进行网络安全的旧方法，引发了对网络安全与MAC地址修改之间关系的讨论。

• glerk提供了另一种MacOS上的命令行方法，并分享了在冰岛航空网络上的实际应用。

• ClawsOnPaws询问是否可以通过快捷方式解决MAC地址修改问题，暗示可能有更简便的解决方案。

• 讨论中涉及多个操作系统（MacOS、Linux、Windows、Android）的MAC地址修改方法，显示出跨平台的应用场景。
• 提到了MAC地址修改在不同场景中的实际应用，如网络安全、隐私保护、绕过带宽限制等。
• 争议的焦点在于使用非法MAC地址（如全零地址）的有效性和潜在问题，以及时间限制WiFi的实际可行性和普遍性。
• 提供了多个工具和脚本的推荐链接，展示了技术社区中对该问题的具体解决方案。

44310763.article_content:
Download Airpass for Mac
Why?
Wifi networks collect a reference to your computer (called MAC address) when you login. That way, when you try to login again, even with different credentials, they detect that it is the same device and do not allow you to continue using it.
How?
By renewing your device's MAC address, the wifi network will not identify your computer and therefore is tricked into thinking it's a new device. When you try to login again it won't trigger the error message and you're free to use it.
Made while ✈️ by
Tiago Alves

data.title: Show HN: MMOndrian
data.author: neural_thing
data.article_summary: 《MMOndrian Rectangles》是由Sergey Alexashenko创作的一款在线互动艺术工具。用户可以通过点击和拖动等操作，对画面进行重新着色、添加或删除线条以及移动和缩放视图。左键点击用于重新着色，右键点击用于添加或删除线条，拖动用于移动线条或平移画面，滚动则用于缩放。该工具提供了简便的交互方式，让用户在抽象几何图形中进行艺术创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某互动应用程序的使用体验和功能反馈

不同观点：
• gschizas：用户无法正常使用该应用，点击没有任何效果，控制台没有错误信息，但能看到一些网络流量（如WSS、XHR）。唯一的反馈是右键点击时显示坐标信息。
• pimlottc：误以为该应用与 Ultima 游戏有关，提到了 Mondain。
• juancroldan：对应用的概念表示喜爱，并好奇是先有应用创意还是文字游戏（双关语）。
• detourdog：询问应用是否使用了DeStijl宣言中的规则来使用颜色和线条。
• ggrelet：怀疑网站是否已经失效。
• Heliodex：对应用给予积极评价，分享了领土占领策略，如选择颜色、占领区域和细分区域等。
• sublinear：到达应用时发现已经被过度细分，有人用颜色写出了“ASS”。
• brulard：编辑的内容很快消失，或者只能维持20秒左右。
• graypegg：收到“连接过多”的错误信息，并表示由于频繁点击感到抱歉。
• dmwood：喜欢该应用，但希望能保存图像为SVG格式，而不仅仅是截图。
• dunham：无法平移，且缩放不会缩放到鼠标位置，但成功写出了"HI"。
• leoff：觉得合并方块最有趣，但遇到服务器拒绝合并的bug。
• thunkingdeep：应用无法正常工作，点击的内容会自动取消。
• remram：删除线条功能不正常，线条会短暂消失然后重新出现。

补充讨论：
• 用户对应用的功能（如平移、缩放、合并方块、删除线条等）存在较多抱怨和bug反馈。
• 有用户对应用的创意表示喜爱，但也对其实现和功能提出了改进建议。
• 服务器负载问题（如连接过多）导致部分用户无法正常使用应用。
• 应用的互动性和策略性（如领土占领、细分区域等）得到了部分用户的积极评价。

data.title: Show HN: lambda-nat-proxy – Serverless proxy using Lambda and UDP NAT punching
data.author: danvittegleo
data.article_summary: **Lambda NAT Proxy** 是一个无服务器代理实现，利用NAT打洞技术通过AWS Lambda函数建立QUIC隧道。其工作原理分为三个阶段：首先通过STUN协议获取公共IP并写入S3桶以触发Lambda函数；然后通过UDP包进行NAT打洞，建立双向NAT映射；最后通过QUIC协议建立加密隧道，用于流量转发。该系统无需EC2实例或SSH隧道，只需配置Lambda函数和S3。用户通过配置SOCKS5代理（localhost:1080）使用该代理服务，流量路径为：浏览器 → SOCKS5 → QUIC隧道 → Lambda → 互联网。系统支持不同性能模式，并自动管理会话和资源清理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在不同技术方案下实现数据处理和网络隧道的成本与技术复杂性

不同观点：
• [pbnjay] 认为使用大量数据通过某些服务（如AWS Lambda）可能会变得相当昂贵，并提出如果在Lambda上实现Tailscale DERP服务器会很有趣。这暗示了对成本的关注以及对技术创新的兴趣。

• [robcohen] 提出了另一种方案，即使用Nix flake生成基于Solo5的微VM镜像，运行MirageOSunikernel，并通过UDP hole punching和relay fallback实现NAT traversal。这种方法可以在Fly.io上部署，作为轻量级、自动扩展的Firecracker VM，并且是按秒计费，成本可能低于Lambda。他质疑使用Lambda的必要性，认为其云无关的方案可能更具成本效益。

• [shayonj] 对[robcohen]的概念表示兴趣，并表达了对廉价且“一次性”的隧道设置方法的渴望，希望减少对出口节点的负担。这反映了对简单易用和低维护成本的解决方案的需求。

• [danfritz] 对整体方案表示兴趣，但更关注实际成本，表明了对潜在高成本的担忧。

补充讨论：

Lambda NAT Proxy
A serverless proxy implementation that uses NAT hole punching to establish QUIC tunnels through AWS Lambda functions. By coordinating through S3 and using UDP traversal techniques, it creates encrypted proxy connections without requiring any dedicated servers - just Lambda functions that spin up on demand.
About
This project evolved from exploring an unconventional idea: can AWS Lambda functions work as network proxies? Building on my earlier
awslambdaproxy
experiment, this implementation solves the performance and infrastructure challenges using NAT hole punching and QUIC protocol. The result is a serverless proxy that needs no EC2 instances, no SSH tunnels - just Lambda functions and clever networking.
How It Works
The system uses a three-phase approach to establish NAT traversal:
1. Coordination Phase
Client discovers public IP via STUN protocol
Writes session info (IP:port, session ID) to S3 bucket
S3 event notification triggers Lambda function
2. NAT Hole Punching
Both client and Lambda send UDP packets to each other's public endpoints
Creates bidirectional NAT holes for subsequent traffic
Uses session ID for packet correlation
3. QUIC Tunnel Establishment
Client starts QUIC server on punched port
Lambda connects as QUIC client through established hole
Encrypted, multiplexed tunnel ready for traffic forwarding
Traffic Flow:
Browser → SOCKS5 → QUIC Tunnel → Lambda → Internet
The Lambda function acts as an exit node, forwarding tunneled traffic to destination servers and relaying responses back through the QUIC connection.
Architecture
┌─────────┐   SOCKS5    ┌──────────────┐   QUIC/UDP   ┌─────────┐   HTTP/S   ┌───────────┐
│ Browser │ ──────────  │ lambda-nat-  │ ──────────── │ Lambda  │ ────────── │ Internet  │
│         │ :1080       │ proxy        │              │ Function│            │ Servers   │
└─────────┘             └──────────────┘              └─────────┘            └───────────┘
│                            ▲
│ session data               │ S3 event
▼                            │
┌─────────────┐                     │
│ S3 Bucket   │ ────────────────────┘
│ (coord)     │
└─────────────┘
Setup
Prerequisites:
AWS CLI configured with Lambda, S3, CloudFormation permissions
Setup:
lambda-nat-proxy config init
Deploy infrastructure:
lambda-nat-proxy deploy
Run proxy:
lambda-nat-proxy run
Configure browser to use SOCKS5 proxy:
localhost:1080
The system auto-detects deployed resources and handles session management automatically.
Commands

Create configuration file

#
Deploy AWS infrastructure

#
Start SOCKS5 proxy server
lambda-nat-proxy status

Show deployment status

Performance Modes

normal

performance

Implementation Details
NAT Traversal Algorithm:
Client binds UDP socket and performs STUN discovery
Client writes session data to S3:
{client_ip, client_port, session_id, timestamp}
S3 notification triggers Lambda function with session data
Lambda binds UDP socket and performs STUN discovery
Both endpoints send UDP packets to each other's public address
NAT devices create bidirectional port mappings
Client starts QUIC server, Lambda connects as client
QUIC connection established for traffic forwarding

Built-in encryption (TLS 1.3)

44302623.article_summary: **Lambda NAT Proxy** 是一个无服务器代理实现，利用NAT打洞技术通过AWS Lambda函数建立QUIC隧道。其工作原理分为三个阶段：首先通过STUN协议获取公共IP并写入S3桶以触发Lambda函数；然后通过UDP包进行NAT打洞，建立双向NAT映射；最后通过QUIC协议建立加密隧道，用于流量转发。该系统无需EC2实例或SSH隧道，只需配置Lambda函数和S3。用户通过配置SOCKS5代理（localhost:1080）使用该代理服务，流量路径为：浏览器 → SOCKS5 → QUIC隧道 → Lambda → 互联网。系统支持不同性能模式，并自动管理会话和资源清理。

data.title: The Art of Bijective Combinatorics
data.author: doubledamio
data.article_summary: 《The Art of Bijective Combinatorics》是一个创新的“视频书”项目，由印度数学科学研究院（IMSc）在2016至2019年间录制。它包括77个视频讲座、对应的幻灯片，以及一个方便导航的网站。该项目分为四部分，涵盖了枚举、代数、双射组合学等主题，并探讨了这些主题在物理学和计算机科学中的应用。每个部分可独立学习，适合高年级本科生和研究生，同时也包含一些高级内容供研究人员参考。视频书提供了详细的描述和链接，允许观众快速找到感兴趣的部分，并结合了视觉数学和动画以增强理解。尽管视频内容保持不变，但网站仍在更新补充材料。该视频书可以像传统书籍一样在文献中引用。

The Art of Bijective Combinatorics
The Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, India Â (January-March 2016-2019)
Foreword
Preface

Some lectures for a wide audience
The Art of Bijective Combinatorics(for short Â  "ABjC")Â is not a book, it is not an e-book, it is not reduced to a collection of videos, it is a kind of "video-book"
This "video-book" Â "ABjC" Â has 3 components:
- a set of 77 lectures video-recorded at the Insitute of Mathematical Science (IMSc), Chennai, India, as a series of four different courses on "bijective combinatorics" during four consecutive years (2016-2019) at the invitation of Amritanshu Prasad Â (Amri),
- the correponding set of slides of each lecture,
- aÂ websiteÂ which enable one toÂ navigate inside the videos, in the same way you turn around the pages of a book. For example if you click on the time given just after the slide number corresponding to one of the videos, you will get, up to one second, to exact position in the video.
an introduction to the video-book ABjC is given at the beginning of the
video of the Epilogue
Â  (from 2' 02" to 8' 42")
This video-book on bijective combinatorics is in four parts (or "volumes"), each part corresponds to a combinatorial course given at IMSc.
part I:
Â  An introduction to enumerative, algebraic and bijective combinatorics Â (January-March 2016)
part II:
Â Commutations and heaps of pieces with interactions in physics, mathematics and computer science Â  (January-March 2017)
part III:
The cellular ansatz: bijective combinatorics and quadratic algebra Â (January-March 2018)
part IV:
A combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials and continued fractions Â (January-March 2019)
A series of courses at two different levels
Each course can be followed independently. There are manyÂ overlaps between the differents courses.Â I gave theseÂ courses at two different levels at the same time. Most of the courses are supposed to be followed by good undergraduate students (at the Master level) and graduate students. I also gave some more advanced topics, opening some Â«windowsÂ» without proof, for graduate students, researchers and professors, in connection with active researches in combinatorics, and sometimes with connection in theoretical physics and computer science. Such sections are listed under the name Â«ComplementsÂ». In this video-book their are some new results and also some new ways to present classical theory.Â These courses were followed by undergraduate and graduate students, together with some professors, in mathematics, physics and computer science, from IMSc and the neighbourless institutes in Chennai: CMI (Chennai Mathematical Institute) and IIT (Indian Institute of Technology) Madras.Â
Book or video-book ?
Â The discussion is open if it is better to write a book (here in fact 4 books !) or "to speak" a "video-book". Nowadays many lectures and courses are recorded in videos.
One of the main disadvantage of videos is that it is difficult to find or listen just a part or a particular point in which one is interested. I tried to overcome this difficulty by giving a detailed description of each video, using the corresponding slides, Â with some direct links going inside the video. Also nowadays, most people give together with a research paper, a set of slides giving a survey of the paper. I found very convenient to look first at the set of slides coming from a talk, and then to the paper in order to go inside the proofs ot the details. Here in this video-book,Â Â I tried to imitate this attitude: first the reader can look at the set of slides, and for more details go to the corresponding portion of the video with the links given in this website.
Â The emphasis of the course being on the bijective point of view in combinatorics, there are many figures, visual mathematics and some animations.Â
Here is the advantage of a video-book, keeping the beauty of bijections and bijective proofs. Although transparencies and overhead projectors had been replaced by video-projectors, I tried to keep the spirit of the so-called Â«ViennotiqueÂ» with Â handmade transparencies in color which are incorporated in the modern techniques. This website is in progress for completing the biography, references, historical notes, index, adding complementary lectures and videos, etc ... The videos and slides will remain unchanged, even if I find some mistakes or errors which will be added to this website.
How to quote this video-book in the literature
The videos, slides and the address of this video-book ABjC will remain unchanged. It is possible to quote this video-book in the literature in the same way as quoting a book.Â Â If you give only the direct link to a set of slides, or to the YouTube address of a video, the reader will miss the corresponding page giving the precise decription of the slides, video and direct links in order to navigate inside the video. data.article_summary: 国会正计划出售超过2.5亿英亩的公共土地，涉及11个州，包括阿拉斯加、加利福尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他等。根据提案，美国森林服务局和土地管理局管理的土地将出售给“任何有兴趣的 parties”，仅有少量保护区可免于出售。这引发了环境保护者的担忧，因为这些土地包括北极、奥特罗台地和奥怀希峡谷等重要生态区域，对野生动物和当地社区至关重要。此外，该法案还涉及在北极保护区进行石油租赁销售和增加国家森林采伐量等条款。批评者认为，这不仅是破坏性的，还开创了一个危险的先例，可能导致更多公共土地被变卖以资助特定项目。公众被呼吁联系参议员反对该和解法案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国公共土地出售提案及其影响

不同观点：
• **jjulius的观点**：jjulius澄清自己并不支持出售公共土地，但指出目前提案仅涉及出售0.5%到0.75%的美国森林服务局（USFS）和土地管理局（BLM）土地，最多不超过1.5%。出售的土地需用于特定目的，且买家需在成本上有效率。尽管jjulius不希望看到这些土地被出售，但认为如Wilderness Society等组织的警告有些夸大。

• **abeppu的观点**：abeppu质疑出售土地以解决住房危机的有效性，指出住房危机并非由于土地不足，而是由于房屋位置不佳或价格不合理。此外，在西部州，靠近或毗邻野地的住房会增加火灾风险，可能导致保险问题。因此，即便不考虑环境或伦理问题，这个提案在实现其声称的目标上也是无效的。

• **linuxhansl的观点**：linuxhansl将公共土地出售与削减医疗补助和为富人减税联系起来，认为此举是为了填补税收缺口。提案可能需要进一步提高债务上限，且提案整体像是一场闹剧。

• **cvoss的观点**：cvoss建议大家直接阅读法律提案文本，而不是依赖某个组织的解读。提案规定，州和地方政府（包括印第安部落）必须参与决定哪些土地出售，且出售的土地必须用于住宅或社区需求。土地不能低于市场价值出售，私人买家需通过竞争性方式购买。

补充讨论：
• **vjvjvjvjghv的观点**：指出这将使户外活动更加困难，特别是在没有“通行权法”的美国西部。提案涉及的土地包含热门 hiking 路线，且出售所得收入可能微不足道。

• **Glyptodon的观点**：以Sabino Canyon为例，说明该地区是Tucson的热门自然景区，周边是高档住宅。出售这样的土地会引发巨大争议。

• **snowwrestler的观点**：解释参议员Mike Lee推动此提案的背景，指出其目的是为犹他州的地方发展提供土地。然而，提案在预算法案中提出，仅为增加收入。一些共和党参议员已表示反对。

• **wingspar的观点**：强调内华达州、俄勒冈州和犹他州的大量土地为联邦政府所有，指出这些州存在私有化压力。

• **darth_avocado的观点**：认为美国拥有大量未开发自然景观，出售土地是短期思维，且收益不大。可以通过减少富人税收优惠获得更多收入。

• **emushack的观点**：提供反对提案的请愿链接，呼吁公众表达反对意见。

• **nemofoo的观点**：分享个人经历，表示在亚利桑那州常在公共土地上露营，担心孩子无法访问这些营地。

• **deepsquirrelnet的观点**：质疑提案是否对普通美国人有任何好处。

• **bfrog的观点**：批评共和党通过为家族、朋友和捐助者牟利而牺牲公众利益。

• **readthenotes1的观点**：对提案中涉及的土地面积提出疑问，指出文章中提到的2-3百万英亩和2.5亿英亩的数字不一致。

争议焦点：
1. 提案是否会有效解决住房危机。
2. 出售公共土地的环境和伦理影响。
3. 提案的收益和实际效果是否被夸大。
4. 提案是否应在预算法案中提出。
