Blog
Congress is making more than 250 million acres of public lands available for sale.
June 16, 2025
By
Nik Kohomban
Home
Articles
Congress is making more than 250 million acres of public lands available for sale.
The pronghorn antelope has one of the longest big game migrations in the U.S.
Mason Cummings/TWS
Share
Share on Twitter
Share on Facebook
Share on LinkedIn
Share via Email
Bill is a disturbing giveaway that sets an extremely dangerous precedent
On the heels of the disastrous House reconciliation bill’s passage, Senate Republicans have unveiled their own poisonous version of the bill that will fund President Trump’s agenda—a bill that calls for the outright sale of public lands as a key element.
The provision in question mandates the disposal of between 2 million and 3 million acres of lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management and Forest Service across 11 states: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington and Wyoming. Alarmingly, the provision contains very limited exemptions—Wilderness Study Areas, Areas of Critical Environmental Concern, roadless areas and critical habitat are all considered eligible for sale.
Based on those limited restrictions, more than 250 million acres of public lands will be eligible to be sold to "any interested party."
To illustrate just how much is at stake, we’ve created a map of all public lands that are now at risk of disposal.

These are not disposable places as some proponents of land sales have claimed, they are some of the most significant intact landscapes in the United States. The Arctic, Otero Mesa, the Owyhee Canyonlands, Snoqualmie forest—these places are vital not only to the human communities in and around them but also to vulnerable wildlife struggling to survive in an increasingly developed world.
This effort is in and of itself entirely destructive—especially when considered with other provisions in the bill that will mandate oil lease sales in the Arctic Refuge, force construction of a mining road through a national park and more than double the amount of logging in western national forests
—but it also sets a dangerous precedent that members of Congress can simply liquidate our public lands to fund their pet projects.
There is no question that this is a crisis point; our senators and representatives now face a critical test. Will they stand for their constituents and the overwhelming majority of the American public who want to protect public lands? Or will they succumb to pressure and give our public lands away to fund tax cuts for the wealthy?

data.title: Solar electricity every hour of every day is here and it changes everything
data.author: ZeroGravitas
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了太阳能发电结合电池储能技术如何实现全天候24小时供电。得益于电池成本的下降和技术的进步，在阳光充足的地区，太阳能已经能够接近97%的24/365全天候稳定供电，且成本低于煤炭和核能。文章指出，只需17千瓦时的电池储能，就能在阳光充足的地方（如拉斯维加斯）实现1千瓦的稳定电力输出。这种技术进步使得太阳能发电不再受限于白天的光照时间，能够为工业用户和公共事业提供持续的清洁能源，从而改变能源供应格局。文章还探讨了不同城市接近全天候太阳能供电的潜力和成本。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

Highlights
17 kWh
1 kW of stable solar power across 24 hours of the day can be achieved on an average day in a sunny place like Las Vegas with 5 kW of fixed solar panels and a 17 kWh battery.
97%
The sunniest regions in the world can get as close as 97% of the way to 24/365 solar – stable supply every hour of every day of the year.
104 $/MWh
Achieving 97% of the way to 24/365 solar in very sunny regions is now affordable at as low as $104/MWh, cheaper than coal and nuclear and 22% less than a year earlier.
About
This report unpacks the concept of 24-hour electricity supply with solar generation — how solar panels, paired with batteries, can deliver clean, reliable electricity around the clock. It compares cities across the world, showing how close they can get to solar electricity 24 hours across 365 days (24/365 solar generation), and at what price. Focused on project-level applications like industrial users and utility developers, the report shows how batteries are now cheap enough to unlock solar power’s full potential.
Executive summary
24-hour solar generation is here — and it changes everything
Solar electricity is now highly affordable and with recent cost and technical improvements in batteries — 24-hour generation is within reach. Smooth, round-the-clock output every hour of every day will unleash solar’s true potential, enabling deeper penetration beyond the sunny hours and helping overcome grid bottlenecks.
On June 21st — the Northern Hemisphere summer solstice — the “midnight sun” circles the sky continuously, providing 24 hours of daylight and theoretically, 24 hours of solar electricity generation. Thanks to advances in battery storage, this phenomenon is no longer limited to the Arctic.
Rapid advances in battery technology, especially in cost, have made near-continuous solar power, available every hour of every day of the year, an economic and technological reality in sunny regions.
Industries like data centres and factories need uninterrupted power to function. At the same time, the rising push for hourly-matched carbon-free energy goals — pursued largely through corporate Purchase Power Agreements (PPAs) — is
increasing the demand
for clean electricity every hour of the day. While solar is now extremely affordable and widely available, its real value will only be realised when it can deliver power consistently to meet the demands of a growing economy, even when the sun isn’t shining.
24-hour solar generation enables this by combining solar panels with sufficient storage to deliver a stable, clean power supply, even in areas without grid access or where the grid is congested or unreliable. While this may not solve every challenge at the grid level, since not all places are as sunny and the electricity demand varies hourly and seasonally, it provides a pathway for solar to become the backbone of a clean power system in sunny regions and to play a much bigger role in less sunny regions.
This report explores how close we are to achieving constant, 24-hour solar electricity across 365 days in different cities around the world, and what it would cost to get there.

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a new BitTorrent tracker in Elixir
data.author: dahrkael
data.article_summary: ExTracker是一个使用Elixir开发的BitTorrent追踪器，目前仍在开发中，但已具备一些功能。它具有高性能、低内存占用（约200MB/1,000,000 peers）、零设置等特点，支持HTTPS、UDP追踪协议、IPv6扩展等BitTorrent增强提案（BEPs）。部分功能如私有种子、WebTorrent支持等尚未实现。用户可通过源码、发布版本或Docker方式运行ExTracker，并可根据需要调整配置。项目采用Apache-2.0许可证。测试实例已在extracker.dahrkael.net:6969上线，具备实时统计功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir项目设计与实现，尤其是与OTP、性能、技术选择等相关的讨论。

不同观点：
• [nesarkvechnep] 认为项目代码过于过程化，依赖ETS和Application，期望看到更多基于OTP的设计。推荐了两本关于OTP设计的书籍，建议作者学习如何使用OTP设计服务。
• [b0a04gl] 分享了自己学习Elixir一周的经历，强调了Elixir对代码风格的影响，例如状态隔离、无共享数据、模式匹配等特性。他认可项目中简单但有效的流程设计。
• [voicedYoda] 对项目表示赞赏，但建议将IO.puts替换为日志记录器，并考虑添加OTel（OpenTelemetry）以增强可观测性。
• [s-mon] 表达了对Elixir的喜爱，并提到正在用Elixir构建通知引擎，对项目表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• [abrookewood] 对项目的运行性能感兴趣，询问其与opentracker的性能对比。
• [quechimba] 分享了自己几年前用Elixir写的简单tracker代码，并表示会查看该项目。
• [arch-choot] 分享了自己用Typescript和Rust实现类似项目的经验，使用Redis作为数据库，并询问项目全内存数据库的设计决策和遇到的问题。
• [TheJoeMan] 请求澄清DHT和PEX的含义，表示在搜索"tracker PEX"时遇到困难。
• [vivzkestrel] 提出了两个问题：HTTPS无法正常工作以及控制台被无用信息刷屏，希望看到HTTP统计数据。
• [jhgg] 询问作者是否考虑将Elixir作为主要工作语言。
• [andyleclair] 对项目代码表示高度赞赏，认为代码质量高，达到了资深工程师的水平。
• [KomoD] 遇到了HTTPS无法工作的问题，并指出控制台被无效参数警告刷屏，虽然功能似乎正常。
• [bavell] 询问项目是否适合作为私人tracker使用。
• [toomuchtodo] 简单表达了对项目的赞赏。

争议焦点：

data.title: Reddit in talks to embrace Sam Altman's iris-scanning Orb to verify users
data.author: elsewhen
data.article_summary: Reddit正在考虑使用由OpenAI CEO Sam Altman联合创立的公司推出的World ID系统，该系统基于虹膜扫描技术，用于验证用户的唯一性，同时保持匿名。随着AI生成内容增多和各国对年龄验证法律的讨论，身份验证技术需求增加。World ID通过扫描用户虹膜生成加密身份，不存储个人信息，能匿名验证年龄等信息。若Reddit采用该技术，用户可通过World ID验证身份，同时保持隐私。不过，非Orb验证的World ID功能有限，Reddit可能对未完全验证的账户区别对待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型的数据更新速度及其对用户行为的影响

不同观点：
• hu3 认为：当前的AI模型如果能够使用更新的数据进行训练，就可以取代其大部分的Reddit使用行为（主要是阅读）。这表明他对AI的能力有较高期望，尤其是希望AI能够提供更实时和相关的信息。
• 潜在反对观点：未明确表达，但可能有人认为即使AI模型用更新的数据训练，也无法完全替代像Reddit这样的社交平台所提供的社区互动和实时讨论的价值。

补充讨论：
• hu3的评论暗示了对AI进步的期待，特别是对实时性和信息相关性的需求。
• 争议焦点可能在于AI能否真正取代传统的社交媒体使用，尤其是当用户不仅仅是为了获取信息，还为了参与讨论和社区活动。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，hu3提到其大部分Reddit使用行为是“read-only”，表明一部分用户可能是内容消费者而非贡献者，这也影响了AI替代的可行性。

The Scoop
Reddit is considering using World ID, the verification system based on iris-scanning Orbs whose parent company was co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
According to two people familiar with the matter, World ID could soon become a way for Reddit users to verify that they are unique individuals while remaining anonymous on the platform.
Talks between representatives of Reddit and World ID parent Tools for Humanity highlight the growing market for new identity verification technologies, as artificial intelligence floods online platforms with inauthentic content and governments around the world consider new age verification laws to prevent children and teenagers from accessing social media.
If World ID becomes one of Redditâs third-party providers, it would be good news for Tools for Humanity, which was founded six years ago with the lofty goal of providing a universal basic income to the world by offering them cryptocurrency called Worldcoin in exchange for scanning their eyeballs with an Orb.
AD
Reddit and Tools for Humanity declined to comment on the talks.
In this article:
The Scoop
Know More
Step Back
Reedâs view
Room for Disagreement
Notable
Know More
In April, Reddit
lawyers sent
formal legal demands to the University of Zurich, whose researchers used AI to impersonate actual users in an experiment on the powers of AI persuasion. And states across the US are
considering
or
passing
new laws that require internet companies to verify the ages of their users.
As a result, thereâs new urgency to find ways to verify some information about people online while also providing the privacy and anonymity that has become a cherished characteristic of the web.
Last month, Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman said AI and age verification laws would eventually force the company to check whether its users are human and of a certain age. Huffman said the company would work with third-party providers to avoid having to collect user information. âWe will do our best to preserve both the humanness and anonymity of Reddit,â
he wrote
on the site.
AD
When World ID users have their irises scanned by one of the companyâs Orbs today, they still get free Worldcoins, which were worth just under a dollar a piece at the time this article was published.
But these days, itâs not the crypto component that makes Worldcoin a potentially important part of the AI industry. Itâs the technology that can verify whether someone is a unique individual.
When Tools for Humanity was just getting started, it needed a way to prevent people from getting more than their share of Worldcoin. Otherwise, users could keep creating new accounts and receive an unlimited supply of the coin. But it also needed to do that without storing any personal information about users.
AD
The system is sophisticated and complex, but somewhat easy to understand. The Orb scans a userâs iris, which is a one-of-a-kind biomarker like a fingerprint. It then creates an encrypted representation of the iris scan and breaks it up into fragments that are stored only on secret servers around the world, kind of like tearing up an impossible-to-decipher treasure map and hiding pieces of it in bank vaults around the globe.
In order to get hold of someoneâs iris scan, a hacker would have to break into each of those servers, reconnect the fragmented data, and then reverse-engineer it back into the original iris scan. Even then, the hacker still wouldnât know whose iris it was.
After the scan, users then get a unique World ID, which is stored in a locally encrypted vault on their smartphones.
World ID users can also verify their age and other credentials anonymously. If the Orbâs built-in age detection software suspects a user is under 18, it refuses to scan their irises.
Itâs also possible to use the World app without using an Orb. But a World ID without Orb verification has limited functionality. Itâs possible Reddit could accept logins with an unverified World ID, but would treat those accounts differently than fully verified ones. A
pilot program
allows users to verify credentials like passports with the World app by scanning it on the personâs local device, so no information is ever shared.
Step Back
If Reddit does begin using World ID, it wonât be the only way to verify oneâs humanity, according to the two people familiar with the matter. Users will have many options.
The number of online verification tools available to internet users are increasing rapidly and all offer various levels of privacy, security, and convenie

data.title: FedFlix — Public Domain Stock Footage Library
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了美国国家技术信息服务局（NTIS）与Public.Resource.Org, Inc.（PRO）之间的合作协议，旨在促进公众获取NTIS收藏的多媒体产品。根据协议，NTIS每月将选取10到20盘非版权录像带寄给PRO，由PRO自费进行数字化处理并制作成DVD拷贝，随后返还NTIS。这些录像带和DVD属于美国政府财产，PRO不得对内容主张知识产权，且双方可自由公开发布内容并保留所有收入。协议期限为一年，任何一方提前60天通知即可终止。内容也可以通过其他合作伙伴提供，任何一方不得擅自转让权利。该合作不构成排他性协议，也不形成合伙关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于FedFlix（或相关资源库）的内容价值和潜在用途

不同观点：
• **mrbluecoat** 对命名的幽默评论：他调侃资源库的名称，认为不如叫“Nedflix”更有趣，暗示对资源库命名方式的不满或调侃。
• **jchrisa** 关注技术实现：他利用FedFlix的API创建了一个简易的目录浏览器，并对互联网档案馆（IA）提供的易用API表示感谢，显示出对技术开发和资源利用的积极态度。
• **pogue** 质疑内容的实用性：他认为FedFlix中的视频内容主要是低质量的短片，尤其是20世纪50年代的B-roll或二战片段，暗示对内容实用性的怀疑。
• **blensor** 提出新想法：他建议创建一个包含AI生成视频和歌曲的免费库，认为这样可以有效利用资源，并解决生成内容不准确的问题，表达了对资源浪费的担忧和对技术创新的期望。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：内容的质量和实用性是讨论的核心。pogue认为现有资源库中的视频质量不高，而blensor则提出了一个新的解决方案，试图解决内容生成中的浪费问题。
• 技术与创意结合：jchrisa展示了技术如何提升资源的使用效率，而blensor则进一步延伸了技术与创意结合的可能性，提出了创建AI生成内容库的建议。

data.title: Infinite Mac OS X
data.author: kristianp
data.article_summary: Infinite Mac现支持运行早期Mac OS X，尤其是10.1和10.3版本，尽管速度不快，但在实际硬件上表现相似。Infinite HD也收录了那个时代的独立软件。作者尝试使用PearPC模拟Mac OS X，因其早期专为x86机器设计。尽管PearPC代码老旧且开发停滞，但其多平台支持和较少使用线程等特性使其相对易于移植到WebAssembly和Infinite Mac。经过几天的工作，成功让Mac OS X 10.2在浏览器中运行，但性能不如DingusPPC，主要因为缺乏MMU缓存导致计算开销大。PearPC更为稳定，但代码不够规范，且通过“作弊”方式实现部分功能。最终，作者仍希望DingusPPC能在长期内成为更快、更稳定和准确的选择。

44323719.article_content:
tl;dr:
Infinite Mac can now
run early Mac OS X
, with
10.1
and
10.3
being the best supported versions. It’s not particularly snappy, but as someone who lived through that period, I can tell you that it wasn’t much better on real hardware. Infinite HD has also been rebuilt to have some notable indie software from that era.
Porting PearPC
I’ve been
tracking
DingusPPC progress since my initial
port
and making the occasional contribution
myself
, with the hope of using it to run Mac OS X in Infinite Mac. While it has continued to improve, I reached a plateau last summer; my attempts would result in either kernel panics or graphical corruption. I tried to reduce the problem a bit via a
deterministic execution mode
, but it wasn’t really clear where to go next. I decided to take a break from this emulator and explore alternate paths of getting Mac OS X to run.
PearPC
was the obvious choice – it was created with the express purpose of emulating Mac OS X on x86 Windows and Linux machines in the early 2000s. By
all accounts
, it did this successfully for a few years, until interest waned after the Intel switch (sadly one of the
authors passed away
around then). I had earlier
dismissed it
as a “dead” codebase, but I decided that the satisfaction of getting something working compensated for dealing with legacy C++ (complete with its own
string class
,
sprintf implementation
, and
GIF decoder
). An encouraging discovery was that
kanjitalk755
(the de-facto Basilisk II and SheepShaver maintainer) had somewhat recently set up
an experimental branch
of PearPC that built and ran on modern macOS. I was able to replicate their work without too much trouble, and with that existence proof I started on my sixth port of an emulator to WebAssembly/Emscripten and the Infinite Mac runtime.
In some ways PearPC not being actively developed made things easier – I didn’t have to worry about merging in changes from upstream, or agonize over how to structure my modifications to make them easier to contribute back. It was also helpful that PearPC was already a multi-platform codebase and thus had the right layers of abstraction to make adding another target pretty easy. As a bonus, it didn’t make pervasive use of threads or other harder-to-port concepts. Over the course of a few days, I was able to
get it to build
,
output video
,
load disk images
, and
get mouse and keyboard input
hooked up. It was pretty satisfying to have Mac OS X 10.2 running in a browser more reliably than it previously had.
Performance
While PearPC ran 10.2 more reliably, it felt slower than DingusPCC. I had spent some time last year making
some
optimizations
to the latter, partly inspired by the
TinyPPC emulator
in
this SheepShaver fork
(aren’t all these names fun?). I
ported
DingusPPC’s benchmark harness and then
set
about
replicating
the
performance
work
in
PearPC
(both emulators are pure interpreters driven by a lookup table, so the process was relatively straightforward). I was able to shave off about 15 seconds from the 10.2 boot time – it helps from a
saving lives perspective
, but is still not enough given that it takes almost 2 minutes to be fully operational. In the end, I copped out and
added a UI disclaimer
that Mac OS X can be slow to boot. I also got flashbacks to the
“is it snappy yet?”
discussions from the early days of Mac OS X – it was indeed slow, but not this slow.
Performance is still not as good as DingusPPC’s – the biggest bottleneck is the lack of any kind of caching in the MMU, so all loads and stores are expensive since they involve complex address computations. DingusPPC has a much more mature
tiered cache
that appears to be quite effective. More generally, while PearPC may be more stable than DingusPPC at running 10.2-10.4, it’s a much less principled codebase (I came across
many mystery commits
) and it “cheats” in many ways (it has a
custom
firmware and
video driver
, and only the
subset
of PowerPC instructions that are needed for Mac OS X are implemented). I’m still holding out hope for DingusPPC to be the fast, stable, and correct choice for the long term.
A Side Quest
I implemented the “unified decoding table” approach in PearPC’s interpreter one opcode family at a time. When I got to the floating point operations, I assumed it was going to be another mechanical change. I was instead surprised to see that behavior regressed – I got some rendering glitches in the Dock, and the Finder windows would not open at all. After some debugging, I noticed that the
dispatching for opcode groups 59 and 63
didn’t just do a basic lookup on the relevant instruction bits. It first checked the
FP
bit of the
Machine State Register (MSR)
, and if it was not set it would throw a “floating point unavailable” exception.
I initially thought this was the emulator being pedantic – all PowerPC chips used in Macs had an FPU, so this should never happen. However, setting a breakpoint showed that the exception was being hit pretty frequently during Mac OS X startu

data.title: AllTracker: Efficient Dense Point Tracking at High Resolution
data.author: lnyan
data.article_summary: AllTracker是一种高效的高分辨率密集点追踪模型，通过估计查询帧与视频中其他帧之间的流场来实现长距离点追踪。与现有方法不同，AllTracker能够提供高分辨率（768x1024）的密集对应场，并可视化为流图，还能在数百帧之间建立对应关系，而不仅限于相邻帧。该模型结合了光流和点追踪技术，使用2D卷积层和像素对齐注意力层进行空间和时间信息传播，具有快速和参数高效的特点（1600万参数）。模型在保持高精度的同时能够扩展到更大规模的数据集进行训练，并提供了详尽的架构和训练方法分析。代码和模型权重已公开。

Code

Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.
Overview
We introduce AllTracker: a model that estimates long-range point tracks by
way of estimating the flow field between a query frame and every other frame of
a video. Unlike existing point tracking methods, our approach delivers
high-resolution and dense (all-pixel) correspondence fields, which can be
visualized as flow maps. Unlike existing optical flow methods, our approach
corresponds one frame to hundreds of subsequent frames, rather than just the
next frame. We develop a new architecture for this task, blending techniques
from existing work in optical flow and point tracking: the model performs
iterative inference on low-resolution grids of correspondence estimates,
propagating information spatially via 2D convolution layers, and propagating
information temporally via pixel-aligned attention layers. The model is fast
and parameter-efficient (16 million parameters), and delivers state-of-the-art
point tracking accuracy at high resolution (i.e., tracking 768x1024 pixels, on
a 40G GPU). A benefit of our design is that we can train on a wider set of
datasets, and we find that doing so is crucial for top performance. We provide
an extensive ablation study on our architecture details and training recipe,
making it clear which details matter most. Our code and model weights are
available.
Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.
Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.
Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.
Native high-resolution dense tracking
Most point trackers operate at either 256x256 or 384x512, and run out of memory at higher resolutions. Our method can operate at 768x1024 on a 40G GPU, and our accuracy reliably scales with resolution. Most point trackers also only track sparse points, while we track every pixel. We only subsample our output for the purpose of clear visualization.

Sorry, your browser doesn't support embedded videos.
Long-range optical flow, visibility, and confidence, in sliding window
AllTracker works by estimating optical flow between a "query frame" and every other frame of a video, using a sliding-window strategy. We also output visibility and confidence. In relation to other point trackers, this flow formulation is our key novelty, and we make sparse methods (of similar speed and accuracy) redundant. In relation to other optical flow models, the key novelty of our approach is that we solve a window of flow problems simultaneously, instead of frame-by-frame; the information shared within and across windows unlocks the capability to resolve flows across wide time intervals.

data.title: LaborBerlin: State-of-the-Art 16mm Projector
data.author: audionerd
data.article_summary: LaborBerlin正在开发一种采用开源技术和常用零件的先进模块化16mm电影放映机，以解决老旧设备不可靠和难以维修的问题。该项目始于2023年3月，计划在2025年9月前完成原型，并在鹿特丹的“Back To The Future”节上展示。项目分为多个阶段，包括高密度LED测试、原型开发及反馈改进。放映机具有可调节高度和倾斜度、多种电源选项、可调亮度和色温的超亮LED光源、支持不同帧率和格式的胶片传输系统，以及广泛的音频和连接功能。团队正在与专家合作，重点开发光源、胶片传输机制和电子设备。最终目标是满足当代电影艺术家和档案保管员的需求，同时保持便携性和灵活性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于老式电影放映机及其现代化改造的讨论，特别是16mm和35mm电影放映机的技术改造和应用场景。

不同观点：
• **支持简化功能，注重实用性**：[ilamont] 认为该项目的一些新功能（如可变速度从 < 1 到 30 FPS）过于小众，增加了项目复杂性。他建议将重点放在简化功能上，专注于制作一个能够播放16mm光学胶片的低成本开源投影仪，类似于曾经的Super 8塑料投影仪。他还提出可以增加一些更实用的功能，如评估胶片质量或清理老旧胶片的工具。
  
• **怀旧情感，支持保留老式技术**：[moonshinefe] 对老式投影机的怀旧情感很深，认为保留这种媒介非常有意义，并回忆了以前在影院操作老式机器的满足感。他对数字投影机的普及表示了一些遗憾。

• **对色彩保留的意外发现**：[luckystarr] 提到没有想到旧16mm投影的褪色不是因为录制不良，而是由于投影机的问题，认为这是一个有趣的发现。

• **对项目工程的兴趣与支持**：[sho_hn] 对项目表示强烈兴趣，并表示自己有相关技术背景，希望能早些参与类似项目。

• **对多帧率支持的疑问**：[gwbas1c] 对项目需要支持多种不同帧率表示好奇，质疑其必要性。

• **对冷却系统的技术建议**：[sandworm101] 对项目中使用AOI CPU冷却器提出了技术建议，指出其潜在的蒸发和空气渗透问题，并建议如何优化散热设计。

• **对LED效率的疑问**：[the_third_wave] 对使用800W LED来达到250W卤素灯泡的亮度表示不解，因为通常LED效率更高，这里的情况相反，他对此提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• **关于胶片存档方法的争议**：[yapyap] 对博客中提到的档案管理员需要16mm投影机的用途提出疑问，认为直接扫描胶片比投影后再拍摄存档更合理。这个问题引发了对胶片存档最佳方法的讨论。

总体来看，讨论中既有对老式电影放映技术的怀旧支持，也有对项目技术细节和实用性的理性分析与建议。争议焦点主要集中在项目功能的复杂性和某些技术选择的合理性上。

LaborBerlin: State-of-the-Art 16mm Projector
Background
While artists all over the world continue to work with celluloid film, they are often confronted with precarious screening conditions due to increasingly old and hard to repair equipment. In particular, film projectors and their aging mechanical parts have become less dependable, contributing in many cases to the destruction of the film material instead of ensuring its optimal presentation. The last 16mm commercially available film projector was built in the 90’s but most artists, archivists and projectionists have to deal with much older equipment, sometimes going back to the 60’s and 50’s. At the same time, the traditional industrial manufacturers have disappeared or shifted to other fields, service personnel have retired and spare parts are rare and unreasonably priced. Designed mainly for standard film projections, vintage projectors also fail to cater to contemporary demands: While not offering enough flexibility for artists who work in expanded cinema, they also don’t usually meet the needs of archival projection. Along with the digital revolution, which has, in the last decade, already greatly reduced the opportunities for experiencing analogue film projection, the aging technology of vintage projection equipment has become an important factor in the disappearance of analogue film projection and the uniqueness of its experience.
Introduction
Our idea is to develop a state-of-the-art and modular 16mm film projector using only open-source technologies and non-proprietary/commonly available spare parts. We believe that especially the central mechanical elements of the old projectors – claw mechanism, shutter wheel and film transport - are in most cases so well engineered that a new development here would be a waste of time and energy. Instead, we want to build the projector on the basis of an existing - and easily available - projector mechanism. The same applies to the optics: lenses that are compatible with projectors made by Eiki, Bauer, Bell & Howell and Hokushin are available worldwide in good condition. This projector should cater to the needs of contemporary film artists, archivists and projectionists alike.
Technical Features (Wish List)
Design
Modular design
Open source technologies
Non-proprietary & commonly available spare parts (3D-printable)
Adjustable height & tilt
Lightweight for travelling & portability during projection
Option to project in vertical format (90° tilted or Prism system)
Power
110V & 220V
Optional: Battery for outdoor & portability during projection
Light source
Super bright, dimmable LED
Color temperature adjustment for differently timed prints,Tungsten or Xenon or redshifted film prints
Digital shutter (flicker)
Film formats
16mm – Super-16 – Ultra-16 – open gate
(with switchable format masks)
Steady focus between print & reversal stocks
Optional: interchangeable sprocket wheels for shrunk film
Optics
Wide zoom range lens 25mm – 150mm
Compatible with Bauer, Eiki & B&H lenses (adapter tubes)
Focus with Worm Gear
Anamorphic lens holder
Holder for Elmo Viewer Type 100 (viewing without screen)
Transport
Crystal sync speeds: 12 – 15 – 16,66 – 18 – 23,976 – 24 – 25 – 29,97 – 30 FPS
Manual vario-speed from < 1 to 30 FPS
Vario shutter wheel independent from FPS
Digital frame counter
Memory counter for in- and out-point
Fast rewind in both directions
Audio
Optical & magnetic audio (no built-in amplifier – just outputs)
Microphone input for live voice
Headphone jack
Integrated digital audio sync system
Connectivity
Sync with digital audio, video & midi
Sync between several projectors
Switchable from master to slave
Sync with Elmo ESS system
Optional: ready for telecine
Remote control: IR / Cable / Bluetooth
Accessories
Development of a compatible looper device
Spool arm extensions
PHASE I
State of the Project – March 2023
Our project takes place over a period of two and a half years, and should be completed by September 2025 with the presentation of a prototype at the Back To The Future Festival in Rotterdam.
As a first step, in a team of two, we disassembled four film projector models, which we found offered a suitable mechanical system that could serve as the basis for further development. We have defined three fields of development, for which we will have to collaborate with different experts. These fields are light source, film transport mechanism and electronics.

data.title: ARIA, the UK's Bet to Build Scientific Revolutions
data.author: almost-exactly
data.article_summary: 《ARIA：英国构建科学革命的尝试》一文介绍了英国高级研究与发明局（ARIA）的使命与运作模式。ARIA常被称为“英国的DARPA”，但并非简单复制，而是受DARPA启发，如采用任期有限的项目主管来领导和管理外部研究团队。ARIA的目标是通过支持大胆、非共识的科学创意，催生重大技术突破，改变人们对可能性的认知。与DARPA不同，ARIA在设立时经过精心设计，确保其独立性和自主性，避免过多政治干预。ARIA与风投公司不同，它更关注高风险、高回报的“可能实现的重大突破”，旨在推动经济、生活质量和全球科技进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国新成立的政府资助尖端研究机构（ARIA）的潜在影响和挑战

不同观点：
• [AnotherGoodName] 认为成立这样的研究机构是理所当然的，并以澳大利亚的CSIRO为例，指出其历史成就和经济回报，如WiFi技术和选择性育种，表明政府资助的研究所能带来巨大收益。

• [nickdothutton] 对ARIA的前景持怀疑态度，认为政府对研发的关注短暂且不稳定，监管障碍是主要问题。以英国在核能研究领域的落后为例，说明英国在多个研究领域面临类似问题。

• [hdivider] 支持ARIA的成立，但希望英国能引入类似美国SBIR/STTR的计划，尤其要避免只惠及精英机构如牛津和剑桥，强调小企业的重要性及其在创新中的巨大影响。

• [ggm] 回顾了英国过去如NPL和Daresbury等研究机构的成就与失败，指出成功的研发需要接受可能的巨大失败，并以DARPA为例，说明持续资金支持的重要性。

• [alun] 肯定ARIA的成立是一个积极步骤，但强调其成功取决于是否能避免短期主义，选择无私且有远见的领导者，以应对长期研究项目。

• [simianwords] 关注ARIA的运作模式，质疑其市场激励机制，尤其是是否像风投公司那样通过股权换取资金支持。

• 对ARIA具体运作模式和市场激励机制的关注，提出了是否采用类似风险投资模式的疑问。

The UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) is often referred to as a “UK DARPA”. While ARIA is no DARPA clone, many features of the agency are admittedly DARPA-inspired, such as the use of term-limited program managers, which ARIA calls program directors. These program directors serve as chief visionaries for their programs as well as fund and actively manage teams of coordinated external researchers towards a program's well-defined goal. Despite these similarities, the founding team at ARIA views their work as a metascience experiment all its own. ARIA’s ultimate aim is to drive economic output, quality of life improvements, health benefits, and innovation in the UK. The strengths, needs, and context of the modern UK R&D ecosystem shape the agency’s structure at least as much as lessons from DARPA history.
Any given ARIA program is meant to catalyze progress towards big-if-true, non-consensus ideas. These programs each represent different bets that fall within what ARIA calls ‘opportunity spaces.’ Opportunity spaces delineate areas that ARIA and its program managers believe might be ideal places to create big-if-true technology waves.The expectation is not that each program achieves positive results, but instead materially “changes the conversation” regarding what’s possible in a space.
To better understand the ARIA experiment, Eric Gilliam, author of the
FreakTakes blog
and expert on the history of R&D organizations, sat down for a three-hour interview with Ilan Gur, CEO of ARIA. Prior to joining ARIA as its first CEO, Ilan was a founding program manager at ARPA-E, the founder of a lithium battery startup, founding director of Cyclotron Road, and founder of Activate. At ARPA-E, Ilan took a special interest in finding better ways to commercialize exciting research. At Activate and Cyclotron Road, he built fellowships that served as perches for researchers working on societally important ‘ hard’ technologies that might not yet be VC-fundable find their feet and begin developing technologies into market-ready products.
This interview was edited for brevity and clarity, but the full transcript and video can be found at
FreakTakes
.
Join Asimov Press. It will always be free.
Subscribe
Eric Gilliam:
ARIA is called a “UK DARPA,” but it’s different in many ways. How is ARIA similar to DARPA, and how is it different?
Ilan Gur:
When ARIA was created, the tagline was, “A DARPA for the UK.” But we were not set up to be a DARPA. DARPA was created in the United States 70 years ago. How that model translates to the UK is not obvious. However, if you want an existence proof of a funding agency doing things differently and having massively transformative outcomes, DARPA is that existence proof.
In setting up ARIA, the U.K. government also went through a very deliberate process to make sure that it had independence and freedoms to be able to do all of the best things that early DARPA was able to do. And I think it's worth calling out that Parliament, civil servants, and others involved in this got this right. There’s not a ton of political intervention. The processes that do exist are reasonable and make sure we’re responsible stewards of taxpayer funds. But they also weren't prescriptive in what ARIA looks like. We have the freedom to build the agency from first principles.
I sometimes say that the UK government set up a “stem cell of an R&D funding agency,” and now we're trying to differentiate it towards something that changes the world.
Fundamentally, we're meant to take bold bets that amplify different parts of the research system in new ways. I think about our programs as funding a constellation of teams that can lead to massively transformative outcomes at the intersection of quality of life and economic growth — not just for the UK, but for the world. That “for the world” bit is really about the scale of ambition that we are talking about.
E:
How are ARIA’s ambitions different from, say, a deep tech venture capital firm’s?
I:
While some VCs are just in it to make money, a lot of VCs see venture capital as a platform to change the trajectory of the future in positive ways. We share that vision. But the big difference between ARIA and VC is twofold. 44338862.article_summary: 《ARIA：英国构建科学革命的尝试》一文介绍了英国高级研究与发明局（ARIA）的使命与运作模式。ARIA常被称为“英国的DARPA”，但并非简单复制，而是受DARPA启发，如采用任期有限的项目主管来领导和管理外部研究团队。ARIA的目标是通过支持大胆、非共识的科学创意，催生重大技术突破，改变人们对可能性的认知。与DARPA不同，ARIA在设立时经过精心设计，确保其独立性和自主性，避免过多政治干预。ARIA与风投公司不同，它更关注高风险、高回报的“可能实现的重大突破”，旨在推动经济、生活质量和全球科技进步。

• [hdivider] 支持ARIA的成立，但希望英国能引入类似美国SBIR/STTR的计划，尤其要避免只惠及精英机构如牛津和剑桥，强调小企业的重要性及其在创新中的巨大影响。

data.title: Denmark's Archaeology Experiment Is Paying Off in Gold and Knowledge
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 丹麦通过允许业余金属探测爱好者上交文物，推动了一项激进的考古实验，取得了丰硕成果。自2020年以来，探测者Ole Ginnerup Schytz在丹麦农田中发现了大量金质圆盘，其中一枚刻有“他是奥丁的人”的护身符（bracteate），将奥丁崇拜的历史提前了150年。这些发现揭示了丹麦过去的面貌，包括庙宇、贸易路线和定居点。丹麦鼓励公众参与金属探测，并与政府考古学家合作，每年上交超过2万件物品，远超邻国的考古成果。这项计划使丹麦在考古研究上领先于其他欧洲国家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：金属探测、文物发现及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [comrade1234] 分享了个人在瑞士一片古森林中每年采蘑菇的经历，并提到发现古代陶锅残片及潜在的洞穴。虽然对使用金属探测器寻找宝藏感兴趣，但因当地法律限制而作罢。他认为罗马人在瑞士活动频繁，但未必在他提到的区域。

• [BurningFrog] 对人们上交维京时代金 artifacts 的行为表示赞赏，并建议应根据金属价值给予奖励，以减少将文物私自保留的诱惑。他认为这样可以避免有价值的发现流失。

• [erk__] 提到丹麦的Danefæ和Danekræ收藏，前者为人造文物，后者为非人造重要物品。Danekræ收藏数量较少，目前仅1054件，且可在网上查看，但生物标本和地质标本未包括在内。

• [biophysboy] 推荐丹麦靠近Kronborg城堡的海事博物馆，馆内有数百件模型船、沉船 artifacts 和高质量的水下照片，建议游览哥本哈根时参观。

• [roger_] 提问探测者上交文物后是否会获得某种证书以表彰其诚实。

• [trhway] 提出使用无人机或自主遥控车悬挂金属探测器的想法，认为在乌克兰大规模排雷后，这种技术可能应用于考古等领域。

• [thaumasiotes] 对Ginnerup发现的带有Odin铭文的bracteate提出不同看法，认为虽然该发现将Odin崇拜历史延长了150年，但罗马人早在几个世纪前就已记录了日耳曼神祇，并使用“Mercury”来指代Odin，这表明神祇本质未变。

补充讨论：
• [countrymile] 提到了一部名为《Detectorists》的英国喜剧，认为它对金属探测工作有独特的英式视角，并推荐给感兴趣的人。

• [wewewedxfgdf] 提到一个带有纳粹符号的文物，但指出该符号早在纳粹采用前1500年就已存在，澄清了符号的历史背景。

争议焦点：
• [thaumasiotes] 对Ginnerup发现的历史解释提出质疑，认为尽管发现重要，但对Odin崇拜历史的解读可能存在误差，尤其是对罗马文献的解读存在不同看法。

整体讨论围绕文物发现、金属探测的合法性、技术应用及历史解释展开，各方提供了个人经验、建议和学术观点。

June 17, 2025
14

Denmark’s Radical Archaeology Experiment Is Paying Off in Gold and Knowledge
The Danish government deputized private detectorists to unearth artifacts buried in farm fields. Their finds are revealing the country’s past in extraordinary detail
By
Elizabeth Anne Brown
edited by
Kate Wong
Kristen Nedergaard Dreiøe (
left
) and Marie Aagaard Larsen (
right
) swing their metal detectors over a field where grain is typically grown in southern Denmark.
Alastair Philip Wiper
O
le Ginnerup Schytz, an engineer in Denmark’s sleepy Vindelev agricultural area, had used a metal detector only a handful of times when he found a bent clump of metal in a friend’s barley field. He figured it was the lid from a container of tinned fish and tossed it in his junk bag with the other bits of farm trash that had set his metal detector beeping: rusty nails, screws, scrap iron. A few paces away he dug up another shiny circle. Someone had clearly enjoyed a lot of tinned fish here—into the sack it went. But when Ginnerup found a
third
metal round, he stopped to take a closer look. Wiping the mud from its surface, he suddenly found himself face-to-face with a Roman emperor. At that point he had to admit “they weren’t food cans,” Ginnerup recalls with a chuckle.
After a brief intermission for an online Teams meeting for work that December day in 2020, Ginnerup dug up 14
glittering gold disks—some as big as saucers—that archaeologists say were buried about 1,500 years ago, during a time of chaos after ash clouds from a distant volcanic eruption created a miniature ice age. Four medallions feature Roman emperors, and several bear intricate geometric patterns. But the real showstopper is an amulet called a bracteate with two stylized designs: a man in profile, his long hair pulled back in a braid, and a horse in full gallop. An expert in ancient runes says she was awestruck when she finally made out the inscription on top: “He is Odin’s man.”
These embossed runes are the oldest known written mention of Odin, the Norse god of war and ruler of Valhalla. Ginnerup’s bracteate, which archaeologists describe as the most significant Danish find in centuries, extended the worship of Odin back 150 years—and it’s all because Ginnerup received a metal detector as a birthday present from his father-in-law.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Many other European countries have prohibited or heavily restricted hobbyist metal detecting, but Denmark has embraced it, creating a system for members of the public to hand over finds to government archaeologists. The result has been an embarrassment of riches, with more than 20,000 items turned in annually in recent years. The curators assigned to identify and catalog the artifacts can’t dream of keeping up, but the fruits of their collective labor are clear: whereas neighboring countries have only vague sketches of the past, metal detectorists have filled in the ancient map of Denmark with temple complexes, trade routes and settlements that would have otherwise been lost to history.
“Private detectorists have rocketed Denmark ahead of its neighbors in archaeological research,” says Torben Trier Christiansen, curator of archaeology at Denmark’s North Jutland Museums. “There’s nothing ‘amateur’ about them.”
Denmark has been inhabited since the end of the last ice age, when nomadic hunter-gatherers from southern Europe arrived following the migration of reindeer and retreating glaciers as early as 12,500 years ago. The ancestors of modern ethnic Danes showed up some 5,000 years ago, journeying from the steppes of what is now Ukraine and southwestern Russia. Their descendants lived in small farming communities across Scandinavia for thousands of years, building megaliths and barrows for their honored dead and making human sacrifices in bogs to appease their gods.
In the early centuries of the common era, these farming communities coalesced into a series of Germanic tribes—the Cimbri, the Teutons, the Jutes, the Angles and the Danes—who became skilled seafarers, explorers and metalworkers. Because precious metals—including silver, gold and the components of bronze—do not occur naturally in what is now Denmark, its denizens had to barter for or steal these metals from abroad. They traded extensively with the Roman Empire, which never reached as far north as Scandinavia.
Detectorist Ole Ginnerup Schytz found this gold amulet, or bracteate, bearing the inscription "He is Odin's man." The find extends the worship of Odin back 150 years. (The swastika design next to the man's head predates the adoption of this symbol by the Nazis.)
Arnold Mikkelsen/National Museum of Denmark

data.title: Balatro for the Nintendo E-Reader
data.author: arantius
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了将2024年最佳游戏候选者《Balatro》移植到一个古老且 obscure 的平台——任天堂E-Reader上的可能性。作者热爱《Balatro》，这是一款结合了扑克和纸牌的单人游戏。作者尝试制作了一个E-Reader上的原型，虽然部分界面和功能是模拟的，但核心游戏玩法已经实现。由于E-Reader的技术限制，如屏幕分辨率和显示数字的限制，完整移植存在挑战，尤其是处理高分和大量不同的Joker卡牌。此外，E-Reader的存储空间有限，无法容纳《Balatro》所有的150张Joker卡牌和大量文本。尽管如此，作者认为通过适当简化和重新设计，仍可能创造出一款保留游戏精髓的简化版。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Balatro游戏的技术实现、游戏体验及其相关争议

不同观点：
• Waterluvian认为32位与64位对得分影响不大，因为Balatro的得分远超uint64的最大值，推测使用了某种数值抽象类型。
• Sram1337建议将分数编码为实际值的10倍，例如将1.5编码为15，从而减少最大得分并解决小数问题，同时需要放弃0.01的卡片。
• Im3w1l认为浮点数是可行的，因为Balatro并不需要每秒进行数十亿次的浮点运算。
• Anyfoo表示不理解Balatro的吸引力，认为其过于简化，几乎是“数字上升”游戏，类似于Cookie Clicker，但Balatro有更多的游戏元素，尽管如此，这种直接的“数字上升”让他感到不太喜欢。

补充讨论：
• Azhenley提到作者曾开发E-Reader上的射击游戏，并表示希望看到更多类似的互联网内容。
• Nate75Sanders分享了Balatro在Commodore 64上的版本链接，称赞其在平台限制下的出色表现。
• Kinduff对Playstack和LocalThunk下架此类移植作品表示遗憾，认为这只会让游戏社区更加壮大。
• Fisherjeff对作者表示同情，庆幸自己早先摆脱了对Balatro的沉迷。

44339025.article_content:
What if the best game of 2024 came out on an old, obscure and weird platform?
I friggin'
love
Balatro. I've put an embarrassing number of hours into it. I also like to make games for the Nintendo E-Reader. The E-Reader was a peripheral for the Game Boy Advance that let you load mini games and "DLC" by scanning cards into it.
The E-Reader attached to a Game Boy Advance (image by Nintendo)
Oh and Balatro is a single player solitaire/poker hybrid game that is super fun. If you enjoy poker, solitaire, or especially trading card games like Magic the Gathering or Pokemon, you should definitely check it out if you haven't already.
A while back, I made this mock up screenshot of what Balatro might look like on the
E-Reader.
A mock up of Balatro on the E-Reader
This mock up was really fun to make. So I decided to take it one step further and make a working prototype of the game. This was also a blast to make!
This prototype is
almost
entirely real. It's a real E-Reader game, and it really plays Balatro. I only implemented just what you see in the video, so it's a very long way away from being a full port of the game.
I said it's almost entirely real because it does fake a few things. The blind selection screen is entirely a mock. You just press A and go into the round.
The blind selection screen is completely mocked
And when you win the round, the win screen is mocked too. You have to win with two remaining hands for it to be believable :)
The blind selection screen is completely mocked
But playing the game within the round is 99% real. I hard coded Fibonacci and Splash jokers, and when it calculates what type of hand was played, it only knows about "duplicative" style hands (ie two pair, full house, three of a kind, etc). My wife was sad to find her straight only got scored as a high card. Doh. Many other things are missing too, but this was mostly due to not wanting to spend too much time on this project more than anything.
Could it be done?
Would it be possible to make Balatro for the E-Reader? I think so.
It would be a challenging project and a good number of concessions would need to be made. But I do think a demaked version that still captures the essence and fun of the game is doable.
Dealing with high scores
An immediate challenge would be the massive scores you can get in Balatro. E-Reader games can comfortably work with 32 bit numbers. So the highest possible score would be 4,294,967,295. Real Balatro uses 64 bit numbers so scores can absolutely go into the stratosphere there. But I think 4 billion is still plenty to have fun and get that Balatro experience.
There's more bad news here. We'll talk about it below in the small numbers section.
But ... the Game Boy Advance's screen is only 240x160 pixels, so fitting such large numbers onto the screen would be a challenge. This is an area the demake would have to be different from the real thing. Something like this would be needed (just a quick mock up).
A UI change to accomodate larger scores
So many numbers
Balatro puts a lot of numbers on the screen.
Number of remaining hands
Number of remaining discards
Current ante
Current round
How many cards remain in the deck
How large the deck is
The level of the hand that is being played
The current chip total
The current mult total
Your money
Your score so far in the round
Your score for the current hand
The goal score to beat the round
Did I miss any? The E-Reader has a collection of
DrawNumber
functions, but the problem is it is limited to four unique numbers. If you try to draw a fifth number with
DrawNumber
, nothing happens.
Even worse, each number can have a max of 5 digits. So just to keep track of your score, would take up 2 of those number slots.
A lot of this can be worked around with sprites and some clever redesigning and careful pruning back of features (this would be a demake after all). I do think this challenge could be overcome, but it would probably be the hardest part of this project.
150 jokers?
Balatro has 150 jokers, and they all do very different things. I think making a full fledged "joker engine" that can handle this is doable. The E-Reader/GBA has plenty of memory for this, and it's easy to dynamically call functions. So logic-wise, I don't think this would be a problem. But each joker needs a card graphic.
Five Joker cards in the demaked style
That would really add up and take up a ton of space. Space is always a concern with E-Reader games. Make no doubt, Balatro on the E-Reader would be a very large game by E-Reader standards. But I'm certain fitting all 150 jokers would not be possible. A careful sub-selection of jokers would need to be picked.
Text
Balatro has a ton of text in it. Similar to games like Magic the Gathering, the rules of the game are literally written out on the cards. Balatro uses little text pop outs for this, but it's still the same idea.
The Wee Joker showing its rules pop up
There would be no way to include all this text into an E-Reader demake. So unfortunately the

data.title: Phoenix.new – Remote AI Runtime for Phoenix
data.author: wut42
data.article_summary: Chris McCord，Elixir的Phoenix框架的创建者，介绍了其最新的项目——Phoenix.new。这是一个全在线的编码代理工具，专为Elixir和Phoenix设计，旨在简化实时协作应用的开发。Phoenix.new运行在浏览器中，提供一个临时的虚拟机环境（Fly Machine），允许用户和代理自由操作而不会影响本地机器。它拥有完整的根访问权限，可以安装软件包、运行程序，甚至修改操作系统层面的配置。该工具集成了VSCode界面和GitHub，并通过Fly.io的基础设施提供私有、可分享的URL和实时预览功能。此外，Phoenix.new使用无头浏览器测试前端更改，实时交互和监控应用日志，显著减少开发中的重复性工作。McCord希望通过Phoenix.new解决将应用快速上线的问题，使其成为构建实时应用的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir/Phoenix框架及其与AI工具、部署平台（fly.io）的结合使用体验

不同观点：
• 正面评价：
  - colecut认为Phoenix和fly.io的结合让即使不熟悉Elixir的开发者也能快速部署应用，这种易用性让人印象深刻。
  - ativzzz指出该创新的两个核心：远程代理的容器化环境和与fly.io的深度集成，认为这将为开发者带来巨大的便利。
  - arrowsmith表示担心Elixir在LLM支持方面落后，但看到这种主动努力感到欣慰。
  - ferfumarma和gavmor对Phoenix框架的强大和学习便捷性表示赞赏，并有意进一步探索。

• 批评与担忧：
  - itsautomatisch对fly.io的UI问题、文档不足、以及缺乏使用计量和支持表示不满，认为性价比不高。
  - jsmo和rustc对fly.io的20美元月费包含的服务细节不明确表示困惑。
  - liampulles担心这种工具会让开发者过度依赖特定平台，并质疑是否能脱离fly.io开发。

• 中立/思辨观点：
  - travisgriggs对AI辅助编程的未来持怀疑态度，认为这种工具虽然能减轻部分工作，但也反映了编程领域的一些问题。
  - losvedir对AI工具在持续项目中的管理能力表示关注，并询问如何有效控制项目状态和上下文。
  - psadri认为AI生成代码的进步可能使得应用开发本身变得不再必要，提出了对未来技术发展的深层次思考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  - fly.io服务的性价比和透明度受到质疑，特别是对于20美元月费的具体包含内容，用户表示困惑和不满。
  - AI辅助工具在开发中的角色及其对传统开发方式的影响引发思考，部分开发者认为这既是机遇也是挑战。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  - 对Phoenix和fly.io结合的易用性及其对新手和经验丰富的开发者的不同影响。
  - 对远程代理环境和AI工具深度集成的技术创新表示赞赏。
  - 对AI辅助工具在持续项目中管理能力和长期技术发展影响的关注。

44328326.article_content:
Author
Name
Chris McCord
@chris_mccord
@chris_mccord
Iâm Chris McCord, the creator of Elixirâs Phoenix framework. For the past several months, Iâve been working on a skunkworks project at Fly.io, and itâs time to show it off.
I wanted LLM agents to work just as well with Elixir as they do with Python and JavaScript. Last December, in order to figure out what that was going to take, I started a little weekend project to find out how difficult it would be to build a coding agent in Elixir.
A few weeks later, I had it spitting out working Phoenix applications and driving a full in-browser IDE. I knew this wasn’t going to stay a weekend project.
If you follow me on Twitter, you’ve probably seen me teasing this work as it picked up steam. We’re at a point where we’re pretty serious about this thing, and so it’s time to make a formal introduction.
World, meet
Phoenix.new
, a batteries-included fully-online coding agent tailored to Elixir and Phoenix. I think it’s going to be the fastest way to build collaborative, real-time applications.
Let’s see it in action:
What’s Interesting About Phoenix.new
First, even though it runs entirely in your browser, Phoenix.new gives both you and your agent a root shell, in an ephemeral virtual machine (a
Fly Machine
) that gives our agent loop free rein to install things and run programs  â without any risk of messing up your local machine. You don’t think about any of this; you just open up the VSCode interface, push the shell button, and there you are, on the isolated machine you share with the Phoenix.new agent.
Second, it’s an agent system I built specifically for Phoenix. Phoenix is about real-time collaborative applications, and Phoenix.new knows what that means. To that end, Phoenix.new includes, in both its UI and its agent tools, a full browser. The Phoenix.new agent uses that browser “headlessly” to check its own front-end changes and interact with the app. Because it’s a full browser, instead of trying to iterate on screenshots, the agent sees real page content and JavaScript state â with or without a human present.
What Root Access Gets Us
Agents build software the way you did when you first got started, the way you still do today when you prototype things. They don’t carefully design Docker container layers and they don’t really do release cycles. An agent wants to pop a shell and get its fingernails dirty.
A fully isolated virtual machine means Phoenix.new’s fingernails can get
arbitrarily dirty.
If it wants to add a package to
mix.exs
, it can do that and then run
mix phx.server
or
mix test
and check the output. Sure. Every agent can do that. But if it wants to add an APT package to the base operating system, it can do that too, and make sure it worked. It owns the whole environment.
This offloads a huge amount of tedious, repetitive work.
At his
AI Startup School talk last week
, Andrej Karpathy related his experience of building a restaurant menu visualizer, which takes camera pictures of text menus and transforms all the menu items into pictures. The code, which he vibe-coded with an LLM agent, was the easy part; he had it working in an afternoon. But getting the app online took him a whole week.
With Phoenix.new, I’m taking dead aim at this problem. The apps we produce live in the cloud from the minute they launch. They have private, shareable URLs (we detect anything the agent generates with a bound port and give it a preview URL underneath
phx.run
, with integrated port-forwarding), they integrate with Github, and they inherit all the infrastructure guardrails of Fly.io: hardware virtualization, WireGuard, and isolated networks.
Githubâs
gh
CLI is installed by default. So the agent knows how to clone any repo, or browse issues, and you can even authorize it for internal repositories to get it working with your teamâs existing projects and dependencies.
Full control of the environment also closes the loop between the agent and deployment. When Phoenix.new boots an app, it watches the logs, and tests the application. When an action triggers an error, Phoenix.new notices and gets to work.
Watch It Build In Real Time
Phoenix.new
can interact with web applications the way users do: with a real browser.
The Phoenix.new environment includes a headless Chrome browser that our agent knows how to drive. Prompt it to add a front-end feature to your application, and it won’t just sketch the code out and make sure it compiles and lints. It’ll pull the app up itself and poke at the UI, simultaneously looking at the page content, JavaScript state, and server-side logs.
Phoenix is all about
“live” real-time
interactivity, and gives us seamless live reload. The user interface for Phoenix.new itself includes a live preview of the app being worked on, so you can kick back and watch it build front-end features incrementally. Any other
.phx.run
tabs you have open also update as it goes. It’s wild.
Not Just For Vibe Coding
Phoenix.new can already build real, full-

data.title: You say 'silo' as if it were a bad thing
data.author: HR01
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术和工作环境中“孤岛”现象的利弊

不同观点：
• Jtsummers：认为作者错误理解了“孤岛”比喻，混淆了保护学术完整性和部门间隔离的概念。Jtsummers指出，孤岛化指的是不同学科或部门之间的隔离，例如物理系和数学系互不交流，这会削弱双方的学术发展。他以计算机科学和系统工程学的隔离为例，认为这种孤岛是自然形成的，但不利于跨学科交流。

• vishnudeva：批评文章中存在过多未经论证的笼统陈述，并指出文章错误地假设了“孤岛”攻击者的动机。Vishnudeva认为，人们批评孤岛现象并不是要让所有学科变成一个整体，而是希望打破不必要的隔离。此外，vishnudeva对文章中关于“孤岛”历史的部分表示欣赏。

• esafak：认为知识的锁闭和完整性保护可以同时具有正面和负面效果。Esafak指出，文章的错误在于将信息流动视为双向的，并认为信息应当自由流动，但需要有监控机制以防止不良信息的进入。他认为，关键在于是否有能力管理信息边界。

• jxjnskkzxxhx：从实际工作经验出发，认为在某些工作环境中，孤岛化是完成工作的唯一途径。这一观点强调了在特定情况下，孤岛化可能有其实际操作上的必要性。

• bigyabai：对文章的结论提出质疑，尤其在人工智能和学术孤岛的关系上。Bigyabai质疑学术孤岛如何能推动范式变革，尤其是在无法看到其内部运作的情况下。他进一步质疑如何验证孤岛化对学术进步的实际影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于孤岛现象是否必然有害，以及在何种情况下孤岛化可能具有合理性或必要性。
• 不同评论者对文章中关于“孤岛”比喻的理解和应用存在明显分歧，部分评论者认为作者误解了这一概念。
• 评论中还涉及跨学科交流、信息流动监控以及实际工作环境中的孤岛化现象等具体问题，显示出对该话题的多角度思考。

• Jtsummers：认为作者错误理解了“孤岛”比喻，混淆了保护学术完整性和部门间隔离的概念。Jtsummers指出，孤岛化指的是不同学科或部门之间的隔离，例如物理系和数学系互不交流，这会削弱双方的学术发展。他以计算机科学和系统工程学的隔离为例，认为这种孤岛是自然形成的，但不利于跨学科交流。

• vishnudeva：批评文章中存在过多未经论证的笼统陈述，并指出文章错误地假设了“孤岛”攻击者的动机。Vishnudeva认为，人们批评孤岛现象并不是要让所有学科变成一个整体，而是希望打破不必要的隔离。此外，vishnudeva对文章中关于“孤岛”历史的部分表示欣赏。

• esafak：认为知识的锁闭和完整性保护可以同时具有正面和负面效果。Esafak指出，文章的错误在于将信息流动视为双向的，并认为信息应当自由流动，但需要有监控机制以防止不良信息的进入。他认为，关键在于是否有能力管理信息边界。

• jxjnskkzxxhx：从实际工作经验出发，认为在某些工作环境中，孤岛化是完成工作的唯一途径。这一观点强调了在特定情况下，孤岛化可能有其实际操作上的必要性。

• bigyabai：对文章的结论提出质疑，尤其在人工智能和学术孤岛的关系上。Bigyabai质疑学术孤岛如何能推动范式变革，尤其是在无法看到其内部运作的情况下。他进一步质疑如何验证孤岛化对学术进步的实际影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于孤岛现象是否必然有害，以及在何种情况下孤岛化可能具有合理性或必要性。
• 不同评论者对文章中关于“孤岛”比喻的理解和应用存在明显分歧，部分评论者认为作者误解了这一概念。
• 评论中还涉及跨学科交流、信息流动监控以及实际工作环境中的孤岛化现象等具体问题，显示出对该话题的多角度思考。

data.title: AI is ushering in a 'tiny team' era
data.author: kjhughes
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在商业和开发中的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• neom：认为与大型语言模型（LLM）对话缺乏与人类交流的深度，特别是在捕捉人类对想法的反应方面表现不佳。虽然LLMs有用，但与有经验的人类相比，解锁细微差别需要更多时间和精力。
• WXLCKNO：通过在个人开发环境中添加AI自动化/增强功能，显著提高了生产力，达到原来的2-3倍，在某些方面甚至达到10倍。梦想使用这种工具和一小群朋友及信任的同事建立一个高效的小团队公司。
• jmward01：认为AI让小团队有可能颠覆行业，类似于1999年的小型创业公司浪潮。小团队能更快地解决问题，相比大公司更具灵活性。
• nemothekid：不完全认同AI导致“管理舰队”的趋势，认为小型团队趋势更多是由于2023年的裁员和缩编所驱动。大型团队扩展和经理层级膨胀的时代正在结束。
• spacemadness：对所谓的大幅生产力提升持怀疑态度，认为目前并没有看到高质量软件的大量涌现。强调需要看到实际成果，而不仅仅是SQL查询自动化等小改进。
• geremiiah：指出AI帮助加速代码编写，但开发人员仍需对代码有良好理解。仅仅加快编写速度并不意味着开发人员可以承担更多责任，否则会导致倦怠。
• satvikpendem：引用书籍观点，指出通过现代工具和网络，个人有可能运行大规模多百万美元公司。AI和LLMs的兴起进一步提高了这种可能性，但技术创始人仍需具备修复代码的能力。
• lpa22：认为AWS和GCP等云提供商在允许小型团队运作方面发挥了重要作用，过去需要10人以上的运维团队，现在可以由AWS完成。
• JaggerFoo：认为文章中提出的想法扩展了人们对AI在未来商业创业和运营中角色的思考，收入 per employee只是次要问题。
• apical_dendrite：基于自身经历，指出最大化收入 per employee 的公司在质量投资上存在问题，导致客户体验灾难性下降。
• aussieguy1234：分享个人经验，利用AI在营销、公司设立、税务和编码审查等方面提供帮助，使得一人公司得以高效运作。
• ryandrake：提出资本主义终极状态的设想，即公司由AI和机器人员工运作，人类仅作为CEO进行“指挥”。这种设想被视为股东的理想状态，以最大化利润。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI带来的生产力提升是否真实且可持续，特别是在软件质量和创新方面的实际成果。
- 小型团队与大型团队的灵活性和效率比较，以及裁员和缩编对小型团队趋势的影响。
- AI在代码审查和质量保证中的实际应用效果，以及对开发人员责任和倦怠的影响。
- 云服务和AI工具如何支持小型团队的运作，使得个人或小团队能够运行大规模公司。
- 资本主义终极状态的假设，探讨AI和机器人完全替代人类员工的可能性和道德问题。

data.title: Show HN: Nxtscape – an open-source agentic browser
data.author: felarof
data.article_summary: Nxtscape是一款开源的智能浏览器，主打本地运行的AI代理功能，注重用户隐私保护。它提供类似Google Chrome的界面，兼容所有Chrome扩展，用户可自行选择API密钥或使用本地模型（通过Ollama）。主要特点包括：隐私优先，数据保留在本地；AI代理自动化任务；开源社区驱动。相比Chrome、Brave、Arc等浏览器，Nxtscape专注于AI增强浏览体验，不涉及广告和搜索业务。用户可以下载安装、导入Chrome数据、连接AI提供商后开始使用。未来计划包括MCP商店和内置AI广告屏蔽器。项目欢迎社区贡献和反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Agentic浏览器的潜在价值、技术可行性、安全性以及市场前景

不同观点：
• **支持并看好Agentic浏览器的潜力**：
   - kevinsync认为，这种浏览器可以作为一个个人助理，帮助过滤垃圾信息、自动化任务、管理浏览内容，极具个人价值。
   - wanderingmind提到，如果这种浏览器能够自动化提取网页上的数据（如CSV文件），将会非常有用。
   - ajb强调了该浏览器在过滤用户不关心的信息（如广告、垃圾内容）方面的潜在价值，尤其是在特定领域（如购物、社交媒体）中。

• **对Agentic浏览器的定义和理解存在疑问**：
   - hannob质疑“Agentic浏览器”是否为一个明确且广泛接受的术语，并认为需要更清晰的定义。
   - ppqqrr指出，目前多个基于LLM的应用正在竞争，浏览器本身并不是关键，而是整个Web的改进。

• **对安全性的担忧**：
   - mullingitover担心这种浏览器可能会带来严重的安全风险，特别是在处理敏感账户信息和不受信任的网络输入时，存在被攻击的可能性。

• **对技术实现和现有产品的比较**：
   - Tsarp建议，是否可以通过现有的强大扩展来实现Agentic功能，而非开发全新浏览器。
   - joshstrange分享了试用体验，指出LLM在处理复杂查询时的不足，并提出了一些技术改进建议。

• **对市场竞争和商业可行性的质疑**：
   - lucasyvas认为，AI浪潮下，浏览器的传统形式将被淘汰，未来的机会在于AI驱动的操作系统。
   - admiralrohan关注项目的盈利模式和硬件需求。
   - deepdarkforest指出，浏览器市场竞争激烈，小团队难以与大公司（如Google）竞争，并认为这种项目可能过于庞大。

• **对用户体验和产品设计的批评**：
   - varenc指出了早期版本中的用户体验问题，如模式切换混乱和功能不完整。
   - dvt批评了使用聊天界面的设计选择，认为这并不是处理生产力工具的最佳方式。

补充讨论：
• **商标和命名问题**：
   - blindriver提到“Nxtscape”名称与“Netscape”过于相似，可能涉及商标侵权。
   - lecro对命名提供了建议，认为应选择更易发音和记忆的名称。

• **LLM的局限性**：
   - joshstrange和varenc都提到了LLM在处理复杂任务时的局限性，并建议通过改进提示和数据结构来提升用户体验。

争议焦点：
• **Agentic浏览器的定义和实用性**：一部分用户对其概念和实用性表示怀疑，另一部分用户则看好其潜力。
• **安全性和隐私问题**：如何在增强浏览器功能的同时，确保用户数据的安全和隐私不被侵犯。
• **技术实现方式**：是通过全新浏览器还是通过现有扩展来实现Agentic功能。

总体而言，讨论围绕Agentic浏览器的潜在价值、技术实现、安全性以及市场前景展开，既有支持的声音，也有质疑和批评。

Nxtscape Browser
Your browser, with AI superpowers 🚀
🌐 Nxtscape is an open-source agentic browser that runs AI agents locally. Your privacy-first alternative to Arc, Dia, and Perplexity Comet.
🔒 Privacy first - use your own API keys or run local models with Ollama. Your data stays on your computer.
💡 Join our
Discord
and help us build! Have feature requests?
Suggest anonymously here
.
Quick start
Download and install Nxtscape
Import your Chrome data (optional)
Connect your AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or local Ollama)
Start automating!
What makes Nxtscape special
Features
🏠 Feels like home - same familiar interface as Google Chrome, works with all your extensions
🤖 AI agents that run on YOUR browser, not in the cloud
🔒 Privacy first - bring your own keys or use local models with Ollama. Your browsing history stays on your computer
🚀 Open source and community driven - see exactly what's happening under the hood
🤝 (coming soon) MCP store to one-click install popular MCPs and use them directly in the browser bar
🛡️ (coming soon) Built-in AI ad blocker that works across more scenarios!
Demos
🤖 AI Agents in Action (
watch video
)
💬 Local AI Chat (
watch video
)
⚡ Productivity Tools (
watch video
)
Why we're building this
For the first time since Netscape in 1994, it feels like we can reimagine browsers from scratch. We saw how Cursor gave developers a 10x productivity boost, yet browsers feel stuck in the past.
You probably have 70+ tabs open right now. You're constantly fighting your browser instead of it helping you. Simple tasks like "order Tide Pods from my Amazon order history" should just work with AI agents.
We believe AI agents should automate your work locally and securely, not send your data to some search or ad company.
How we compare
vs Chrome
While we're grateful for Google open-sourcing Chromium, but Chrome hasn't evolved much in 10 years. No AI features, no automation, no MCP support.
vs Brave
We love what Brave started, but they've spread themselves too thin with crypto, search, VPNs. We're laser-focused on AI-powered browsing.
vs Arc/Dia
Many loved Arc, but it was closed source. When they abandoned users, there was no recourse. We're 100% open source - fork it anytime!
vs Perplexity Comet
They're a search/ad company. Your browser history becomes their product. We keep everything local.

We'd love your help making Nxtscape better!

• **Agentic浏览器的定义和实用性**：一部分用户对其概念和实用性表示怀疑，另一部分用户则看好其潜力。
• **安全性和隐私问题**：如何在增强浏览器功能的同时，确保用户数据的安全和隐私不被侵犯。
• **技术实现方式**：是通过全新浏览器还是通过现有扩展来实现Agentic功能。

总体而言，讨论围绕Agentic浏览器的潜在价值、技术实现、安全性以及市场前景展开，既有支持的声音，也有质疑和批评。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新闻链接中提到的AI生成内容的监管和其对社会影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持对AI生成内容进行严格监管。  
  - 论据：AI生成内容可能被用于恶意目的，如虚假信息、欺诈等，因此需要通过法律和技术手段加以限制和管理。  
  - 例子：有人提到Deepfake技术对社会信任的负面影响，认为监管可以有效减少这些技术的滥用。

• 观点二：反对过度监管，认为应鼓励技术创新。  
  - 论据：过度监管可能抑制创新，限制AI技术在各个领域的应用潜力。  
  - 例子：有评论指出，互联网的发展初期也面临类似问题，过度监管可能导致错失技术进步带来的机遇。

• 观点三：对AI生成内容进行标识和透明化。  
  - 论据：通过技术手段对AI生成内容进行标识，让用户能够区分真实内容和AI生成内容，从而自主判断信息的可靠性。  
  - 例子：有人建议采用类似于食品标签的机制，对AI生成内容进行明确标识。

• 观点四：质疑监管的实际可操作性。  
  - 论据：监管AI生成内容的实际操作难度大，技术上难以实现全面监控，且不同国家和地区对内容监管的标准和法律不同。  
  - 例子：评论中有人提到，全球化和互联网的无国界特性使得统一监管标准难以实施。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何平衡技术创新与社会安全。支持监管者担心AI技术的滥用对社会稳定和信任的破坏，而反对者则强调创新的重要性和监管的难度。
- 有评论提到公众教育的重要性，认为提高公众对AI技术的认知和鉴别能力，比单纯依赖监管更为有效。
- 讨论中还涉及对技术中立性的关注，认为技术本身无善恶之分，关键在于使用技术的人的意图和行为。

44340636.article_content:
Fully documented source code for Elite, Revs, Lander, Aviator and more
My name is Mark Moxon and I'm a software archaeologist and reverse engineer. I love analysing old code, and my aim is to create the best code disassemblies you have ever seen. These are my projects:
Elite on the 6502
contains fully documented source code for this seminal space sim from 1984, including 130 deep dives into the code and lots of interesting Elite hacks. Covers the BBC Micro, Acorn Electron, Commodore 64 and NES versions.
Aviator on the BBC Micro
dissects and documents Geoff Crammond's first simulator, analysing everything from the aerodynamic model of the Spitfire to the flicker-free drawing routines.
Revs on the BBC Micro
examines every single instruction in Geoff Crammond's masterpiece, which is regarded as the grandfather of modern racing sims and is still mind-blowing today.
Lander on the Acorn Archimedes
pulls apart the first ever game for the ARM platform, which also happens to be David Braben's second masterpiece (after Elite, of course).
Acornsoft box screenshots
contains every box screenshot from every Acornsoft game. Each screenshot has been carefully reconstructed, pixel by pixel and entirely by hand, using scans of the original boxes, magazines and brochures for reference.
I post updates and announcements about my projects to
Mastodon
and
Bluesky
, and there's also an
RSS feed of my Mastodon posts
.
If you'd like to find out more, then you might enjoy watching
my talks and presentations
.
If you want to know how I create my disassembly websites and repositories, check out the section on
creating my disassembly websites
.
Right on, Commanders!
Mark Moxon

data.title: Good at the Job, Bad at the Interview: Time to Rethink Hiring
data.author: penguin_booze
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了传统面试方法的系统性缺陷，特别是在面试表现与实际工作能力不匹配的情况下。作者是一位有丰富实践经验和成果的领导者，但在面试中常常感到表现不佳，部分原因是作者患有 dyslexia（阅读障碍），在高压环境下难以快速给出结构清晰的回答。文章指出，面试往往更看重候选人在短时间内表现出的自信和口才，而非实际工作中的持续表现和能力。这导致一些在工作中表现出色的人因为不擅长面试而被淘汰，尤其是神经多样性（neurodivergent）的候选人。作者通过亲身经历说明，面试中表现优异的人在实际工作中可能并不如预期，因此需要重新思考和改进招聘方式，避免因面试表现错失真正的人才。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：面试中要求求职者扮演销售角色是否合理

不同观点：
• MongooseStudios认为面试中要求求职者扮演销售角色是不合理的，表达了对这种面试方式的疲惫。他认为面试应该更关注求职者的实际技能和经验，而不是让他们推销自己或产品。
• 另一种隐含观点是，部分面试官可能认为让求职者在面试中扮演销售角色可以有效评估其沟通能力、说服力以及在压力下工作的能力。这种方法可能被视为评估候选人是否适合某些职位（尤其是销售或客户 facing roles）的有效手段。

补充讨论：
• MongooseStudios对这种面试方式感到厌倦，表明这种做法可能已经广泛存在，并且没有达到预期效果。
• 没有直接的反对观点出现在该评论中，但可以推测，有些求职者可能认为这种面试方式有助于展示自己的多方面能力，尤其是在需要销售技巧的职位上。

争议焦点：面试中要求求职者扮演销售角色是否能有效评估其真实能力和适应性，还是仅仅增加了不必要的负担和压力。

44339178.article_content:
I’ve managed multi-site teams, turned around underperforming businesses, trained store managers, and rebuilt HR systems from the ground up. I’ve led in high-pressure environments and helped others grow into leadership roles. On paper and in practice I know what I’m doing.
But put me in a job interview, and everything changes.
Despite years of hands-on experience and proven results, I often walk out of interviews feeling like I’ve underperformed. I ramble. I second-guess the question. I forgot the key example I meant to give. Sometimes I don’t hit the point clearly enough; other times, I over-explain. It’s not nerves. It’s how my brain works. As someone with dyslexia, processing information quickly and delivering sharp, structured answers under artificial pressure isn’t always natural.
And here’s the truth: I’m not alone. There are countless professionals who thrive in the role but struggle in the room.
Yet we keep pretending interviews are the best tool we’ve got.
This is not a matter of personal grievances. I’ve been fortunate to land great roles, build a career I’m proud of, and help others succeed, too. But I’ve also been overlooked for jobs where I was clearly the most qualified because someone else simply “interviewed better”.
It’s time we talked about this. Because if we’re filtering out people based on how they perform in a high-pressure conversation, not how they’ll perform in the job, we’re making hiring harder than it needs to be, and we’re losing real talent in the process.
The One That Stuck
Several years ago, I went for a store manager role at a mobile phone shop in my local town. I had the background and years of experience running high-performing teams, meeting sales targets, and solving real operational problems. I knew I could do the job because I’d done it before, many times, in tougher conditions.
I got to the final two.
The other candidate was someone I vaguely knew—an acquaintance from the local area. He had the chat. Charismatic, confident, and sharp on his feet. During the interview, he made a strong impression and even managed to sell a phone on the spot. That kind of flair tends to impress interviewers.
And it worked. He got the job.
But as I suspected, the reality was very different from the performance. He lacked the consistency and conviction to be professional and reliable day-to-day. He was frequently late. Sometimes the shop didn’t even open. Team morale dropped. Customers drifted. Eventually, the store under his management became one of the first to close in the area.
It wasn’t personal—it was structural. The interview rewarded his ability to sell himself, not his ability to run a store.
That experience stuck with me—not out of bitterness, but because it exposed something we don’t talk about enough: interviews can reward the wrong things. They measure how well someone performs under pressure for 45 minutes—not how well they’ll perform across 45 weeks.
And if hiring decisions are based on who sounds right rather than who is right, we risk making choices that cost businesses far more in the long run.
The Systemic Flaw in Traditional Interviews
The problem isn’t just that interviews are difficult for some people—it’s that the traditional interview model is deeply flawed. It assumes the ability to speak well under pressure is a good predictor of job performance. In reality, that’s rarely true.
1. Interviews reward confidence over competence.
We’ve all seen it—candidates who say all the right things in the room but struggle once they’re in the role. It’s easy to be persuasive for 30 minutes. But real jobs aren’t about delivering polished soundbites—they’re about consistency, follow-through, and practical action. Yet we still equate strong interview performance with capability, even when the job has very little to do with how well someone presents themselves under scrutiny.
2. Interviews disadvantage neurodivergent candidates.
For those of us who are neurodivergent, the issue isn’t knowledge or experience—it’s how our brains process and communicate that information, especially under pressure. And interviews, by design, prioritise quick verbal responses, linear structure, and polished language. That’s not how all of us operate.
I’m dyslexic. I’ve led multi-site teams, turned around failing businesses, and delivered real impact in tough environments. I’m confident. I hold myself well in a room. But in interviews, I often struggle to express what I know in a clear and concise way. I can overthink, over-explain, or lose the thread of what I’m trying to say.
In one recent interview, I was asked if I had experience in the fuel sector. I said no, but that I was a fast learner and had transferable skills. It was a reasonable answer—except it wasn’t true. I do have experience in that sector. I just didn’t manage to access the right words at the right time. And that answer may have cost me the role.

data.title: About Plasma's X11 Session
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了KDE Plasma团队对X11支持的计划。目前，Plasma的X11会话仍在维护中，严重问题会得到修复，但不大会添加新功能或修复较小的问题，除非有人付费。由于X11在多显示器、高DPI、安全性等方面表现不足，转向Wayland是大势所趋。不过，Plasma何时完全放弃X11尚无明确时间表，可能还需要几年时间。大多数主流Linux发行版已默认使用Wayland，且数据显示多数Plasma用户也已转向Wayland。尽管Wayland并非完美，但在多数重要方面优于X11。团队会尽量维持X11支持，直到所有用户都能顺利过渡到Wayland。

44338968.article_content:
Nate
Inside KDE
,
Planning
June 21, 2025
3 Minutes
X11 is in the news again, so I thought it would make sense to be clear about the Plasma team’s plans for X11 support going forward.
Current status:
Plasma’s X11 session continues to be maintained.
Specifically, that means:
We’ll make sure Plasma continues to compile and deploy on X11.
Bug reports about the Plasma X11 session being horribly broken (for example, you can’t log in) will be fixed.
Very bad X11-specific regressions will probably be fixed eventually.
Less-bad X11-specific bugs will probably not be fixed unless
someone pays for it
.
X11-specific features will definitely not be implemented unless
someone pays for it
.
This is actually not too bad; there are relatively few
open and fixable X11-specific bugs
(0.76% of all open bug reports as of the time of writing), and when I went looking today, there were only two Bugzilla tickets requesting new X11-specific features that needed closing. Most bugs and features are platform-agnostic, so X11 users will benefit from all of these that get fixed and implemented.
Eventually it’s lights out for X11 though, right? When will that happen?
Yes, the writing is on the wall. X11’s upstream development has dropped off significantly in recent years, and X11 isn’t able to perform up to the standards of what people expect today with respect to support for multi-monitor setups, high DPI monitors, HDR, VRR, other fancy monitor features, multi-GPU setups, screen tearing, security, crash robustness, input handling, and more.
As for when Plasma will drop support for X11? There’s currently no firm timeline for this, and I certainly don’t expect it to happen in the next year, or even the next two years. But that’s just a guess; it depends on how quickly we implement everything on
https://community.kde.org/Plasma/Wayland_Known_Significant_Issues
. Our plan is to handle everything on that page such that even the most hardcore X11 user doesn’t notice anything missing when they move to Wayland.
Why are you guys doing this? Why don’t you like X11 anymore?
The Plasma team isn’t emotional about display servers; it’s just obvious that X11 is in the process of outliving its usefulness. Someday Wayland will be in this boat too; such is the eventual fate of all technologies.
In addition to the fact that Wayland is better for modern hardware, maintaining code to interact with two display servers and session types is exactly as unpleasant as it sounds. Our resources are always limited, so we’re looking forward to the day when we can once again focus on programming for a single display server paradigm. It will mean that everything else can improve just a little bit faster.
Regardless of when you pull the trigger, isn’t it premature?
Most major distros have already moved their Plasma sessions to Wayland by default, including Arch, Fedora, KDE neon, Kubuntu, and generally their downstream forks. Several others whose roadmaps I’m familiar with plan to do so in the near future.
At this point in time, our telemetry says that a majority of Plasma users are already using the Wayland session. Currently 73% of Plasma 6 users who have turned on telemetry are using the Wayland session, and a little over 60% of
all
telemetry-activating users (including Plasma 5 users) are on Wayland.
Interestingly, the percentage of Plasma 6 users on Wayland was 82% a month ago, and now it’s down to 73%. What changed? SteamOS 3.7 was released with Plasma 6 and the X11 session still used by default! Interestingly, since then the Wayland trendline has continued to tick up; a month ago the percentage of Wayland users dropped from 82% to 70%, and now today it’s up to 73%.
So you can see that to a large extent, this is up to distros, not us. It wouldn’t make sense for us to get rid of Plasma’s X11 support while there are still major distros shipping it by default, and likewise, it won’t make sense for us to keep it around long after those distros have moved away from it.
Regardless, Wayland’s numbers are increasing steadily, and I expect upward bumps when the next Debian and Kubuntu LTS releases come out, as both are currently planned to be Wayland by default.
Now, is Plasma’s Wayland session perfect? No. (what is?)
Is it better than the X11 session in literally every way? Also no.
Is it better in most ways that matter to most people? The numbers say yes!
Well I’m not a most people! I’m me, I’m an individual! I’m not a number, I’m a free man!
That’s fine, and you’re the reason why we’re still maintaining the X11 session! We’re going to try very hard not to to get rid of it until you’re happy too.
Ultimately that’s the goal here: make everyone happy! This includes people who have high DPI 240Hz VRR monitors or laptop touchpads, as well as people using AutoKey or graphics tablets with dials on them. Long transitions like this are tough, but ultimately worth it so that we all get something better in the end.

About
Composers and orchestras like to use their lowest instruments sparingly, for maximum impact. Few instruments go lower and are used more sparingly than the huge and strange octobass, one of the rarest classic instruments in existence.
Invented in 1850 by Jean-Baptiste Vuillaume, the octobass was intended to bring an extremely deep rumble to the orchestra sound. The three-stringed instrument stands between 11 and 12 feet tall, about twice the height of a double bass. This giant bass produces sound so low, some of the notes fall outside the range of human hearing—these vibrations can only be felt.
The rare instrument is almost too large to play. The strings are too big to press with your fingers, so fretting them requires operating pedals and levers that control capo-like mechanisms to press down the strings. In fact, the octobass originally required two people to play: one on the bow (which, though shorter that the bow of a double bass, is extra heavy) and one working the lever system.
Vuillaume originally built three octobasses, two of which are still around. Including contemporary, playable replicas, there are only seven known examples of the instrument in the world, mostly kept in museums, including one at the Musical Instrument Museum in
Phoenix
,
Arizona
. The octobass in Phoenix is tuned C0, G0, D1, a range that's two octaves below the cello and one octave below the modern double bass. Its low C note is lower than the lowest note on an 88-key piano, and beyond what most people can hear (
you can give it a listen here
).
The
Montreal
Symphony Orchestra is the only orchestra that owns one of these unusual instruments, and composers still write music for it on occasion. When played today, it is usually by a single person.
